title: Diezani, Patriarchy And The Politics Of Punishment - Bolouere Opukiri
main_content:
Thread Title: Diezani, Patriarchy And The Politics Of Punishment - Bolouere Opukiri

Main Post: Boardroom to Battleground: Diezani, Patriarchy, and the Politics of PunishmentBolouere OpukiriA stone has the same mass on Earth as it does on the Moon, but it does not weigh the same. Mass is constant; weight depends on gravity. That distinction helps explain the Diezani Alison Madueke saga. The mass of any criminal case should be evidence: documents, payment trails, credible testimony and proof that survives cross examination. But the weight attached to a case often comes from elsewhere: politics, media heat and, in the case of powerful women, patriarchal anxiety.That is why Diezani’s story matters beyond her as an individual. It is not simply a Nigerian corruption. case. It is also a case study in how politics turns women in power into symbols that carry a society’s.wider anger about corruption, elite excess and state failure. In Nigeria, women are increasingly. accepted as executives and technocrats. Politics remains the arena in which many are still treated as trespassers.This pattern is not unique to Nigeria, only more visible in some places than others. In societies where education is broader, social norms have evolved further and white-collar professional culture is more. deeply rooted, women generally find it easier to exercise .authority without being treated as anomalies..Where those transitions are weaker or more .uneven, female power is still read more readily as disorder, rebellion or trespass. Even in .advanced democracies, women in politics are judged more. heavily on personality and likeability than many men. The difference is often one of degree, not kind.Part of the reason lies in the difference between corporate and political power. Education .and white. collar work have made it easier for women to gain authority in structured institutions. In professional. settings, power is mediated through qualifications, internal rules, measurable performance and formal. hierarchies. Sexism remains, but competence is easier to see and defend. That is why women have. achieved more visible success in boardrooms and firms than in electoral politics.Diezani herself embodied that corporate route to legitimacy. She earned a degree in Architecture from. Howard University in the United States, later obtained an MBA from Cambridge University in the United. Kingdom, joined Shell in 1992, and rose through technical and managerial roles until she became the first. woman appointed Executive Director in Shell Nigeria’s history. She later became Minister of Petroleum Resources and, in 2014, the first female President of OPEC. Whatever one’s view of her tenure, she was no accidental figure.But the boardroom and the political arena do not resolve conflict in the same way. Corporate life leans more heavily on numbers, technical skill, audited performance and .institutional process. Politics is harsher because it depends less on technical precision and more on mass persuasion, coalition building, patronage, symbolic dominance and the management of conflict between competing interests. Success in politics often turns not on who has the best résumé, but on who can assemble loyalties, survive attacks and command emotion.That is especially true in much of West Africa, where politics still often sits close to patronclient networks, ethnic balancing, party godfathers, security influence, youth mobilisation and the distribution of state access. Formal democratic structures exist, but informal power frequently remains decisive. Elections are not only contests of ideas; they are also contests over networks, presence, mobilisation and protection.That is why politics is often harsher for women than the corporate workplace. Men who enter it often have easier access to the hidden infrastructure of coercion — thugs, patronage brokers, security contacts, party enforcers and, in some regions, militants who can intimidate, protect or retaliate. Women rarely inherit the same channels. And when they try to build them, they are judged twice over: first as dangerous politicians, then as women who have stepped outside acceptable femininity. Many are therefore expected to compete in an arena shaped by force without equal access to the informal instruments through which force is organised.Seen in that light, Diezani’s trajectory becomes more revealing. She moved from a corporate system into a political order in which power was less about procedure than about who could command loyalty, absorb attack and survive attrition. A woman who could be accepted as an oil executive could still be turned into a national cautionary tale as a politician.Her tenure was also about control over one of the largest concentrations of economic power in the. country. As petroleum minister, she was associated with the drive to deepen Nigerian participation in the oil and gas sector through local-content policy. Nigerian and Niger Delta stakeholders publicly urged stronger enforcement of local-content rules, and she defended awarding a majority of crude term contracts to indigenous firms as part of a deliberate effort to deepen Nigerian participation in the sector. Those reforms shifted opportunities toward local firms and created friction for international operators and entrenched intermediaries. A 2022 study in Energy Policy used Shell Companies in Nigeria’s contract data and an in-country spend model to estimate that contracts awarded to Nigerian companies by Shell alone contribute about $5.6 billion — roughly ₦5.6 trillion — to Nigeria’s GDP each. year. That is the scale of value around which local-content conflict was organised.This helps explain the shape of the public narrative around her. The most viral stories were rarely about regulatory disputes or institutional design. They were about Harrods, jewellery, shopping and spectacle. The diamond-bra story was false, yet it endured because it was too symbolically useful to die. It turned a politically consequential woman into a .cartoon of feminised excess That was not incidental. It was a.form of softer political violence. Not every attack arrives .through physical force. Some arrive as. headlines, rumours, memes and morality tales designed to make one woman carry the dirt of an entire. system. The men around the same networks often fade into the background, while she absorbs the. moral weight.None of this means women should be shielded from scrutiny. It means scrutiny must be evidence-based, proportionate and equal. If Nigeria wants more of its most educated and accomplished women to move from corporate leadership into politics, it must confront a .political culture in which informal coercion still shapes conflict, and in which a woman in power can too easily become the symbolic. vessel for a nation’s accumulated anger.The real question raised by the Diezani saga is larger than one defendant or one verdict. It is whether Nigeria is willing to judge women in politics by the same evidential standards and within the same moral frame it increasingly applies to women in other fields of power. A democracy that welcomes women. into boardrooms but punishes them when they approach sovereign authority is not testing merit. It is. defending an old monopoly.Bolouere Opukiri is a Communications Consultant based in abuja[LINK]

title: New Pledge, Old Lies – Nigerians Slam Tinubu Over Unfulfilled Campaign Promises
main_content:
Thread Title: New Pledge, Old Lies – Nigerians Slam Tinubu Over Unfulfilled Campaign Promises

Main Post: As Nigerians anticipate the manifestos of presidential candidates ahead of the January 16, 2027, presidential election, some citizens, especially opposition figures, have slammed the President Bola Tinubu-led administration for allegedly failing to fulfil promises made by the All Progressives Congress (APC) before the 2023 election.[i]DAILY POST reports that President Bola Tinubu, who assumed office with his Renewed Hope Agenda, promised to tackle insecurity, revitalise the economy, create jobs, improve electricity supply, reduce poverty and thereby improve the living conditions of all Nigerians.[/iThe Tinubu-led administration has claimed that its infrastructure development, investment and social intervention programmes being implemented across parts of the country are game changers and have significantly revived the nation’s economy.However, the renewed political season has brought old promises back into public debate, with critics questioning whether the benefits of the administration’s policies have reached ordinary Nigerians.The opposition claimed that the administration’s policies, including the removal of the fuel subsidy and the floating of the local currency, plunged millions of Nigerians into hardship.According to the IMF’s 2026 Article IV consultation, poverty reached 63% at the national poverty line, while conditions remain difficult for many Nigerians.Tinubu’s promises in 2022DAILY POST recalls that in 2022, President Tinubu released an 80-page policy document that highlighted an eight-point agenda, raising hopes that the economic hardship caused by policies of the previous government might fade away in no distant time. The manifesto included commitments on jobs, electricity, security, infrastructure, agriculture and other sectors.In the eight-point agenda contained in his manifesto, Tinubu promised to create millions of jobs for unemployed Nigerian youths while ensuring that other sectors of the nation’s economy were also revived.Reports indicate that while there have been significant positive changes in parts of the economy, several Nigerians have been plunged into hardship.Job creationPresident Tinubu, in 2022, pledged that if elected Nigerian President, he would “build a Nigeria, especially for our youth, where sufficient jobs with decent wages create a better life”.He pledged to support Nigerian youths and women by “harnessing emerging sectors such as the digital economy, entertainment and culture, tourism and others to build the Nigeria of tomorrow, today”.Although statistics from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) indicate that Nigeria’s official unemployment rate, which was 5.3% in the fourth quarter of 2022, has dropped to around 4.3% to 4.9% in 2026, opposition parties claimed that unemployment remains a major crisis in the country.Affordable electricityIn 2022, Tinubu promised to “generate, transmit and distribute sufficient, affordable electricity to give our people the requisite power to enlighten their lives, their homes, and their very dreams”.During the campaign, the President promised that his administration would provide constant electricity, stating that Nigerians should not vote for him for a second term if they did not have constant electricity supply as promised.In a video clip which is still going viral, the President was captured telling his supporters that there must be constant electricity supply, stating that a promise made must be a promise kept.He said, “by all means necessary, you must have electricity and you will not pay for an estimated bill anymore. If I don’t keep the promise and I come back for the second term, don’t vote for me”.Although the frequent grid failures recorded under previous administrations have been significantly reduced, some Nigerians who spoke with DAILY POST at the weekend dismissed any improvement in electricity supply.Nigerians have continued to lament poor electricity supply across various parts of the country, with some communities experiencing prolonged periods of total blackout.SecurityPrior to his victory in 2023, Tinubu, in his manifesto, promised to establish a “bold and assertive policy that will create a strong yet adaptive national security architecture and action to obliterate terror, kidnapping, banditry, and all other forms of violent extremism from the face of our nation”.However, the security crisis in the country took another turn for the worse in the last three years of the administration.DAILY POST reports that no fewer than 750 people were killed by terrorists in 2025, with several other unsuspecting citizens evicted from their ancestral homes due to persistent attacks by terrorists, bandits and other criminal elements.Nigeria was recently ranked the fourth-worst country in the world in terms of the impact of terrorism.About 12,365 kidnapping incidents have been recorded in the country since Tinubu assumed office in May 2023.A total of 842 people have reportedly been killed across 156 incidents recorded so far this year.At least nine mass abductions have been recorded in the last three years of the Tinubu-led administration, with 551 schoolchildren and staff kidnapped for ransom.Some Nigerians who spoke with DAILY POST warned the APC against launching another campaign with what they described as fake promises.They made Nigerians poor and enriched themselves — ADC chieftainSpeaking in an interview with DAILY POST, the immediate past Chairman of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Rivers State, Leader Sampson, said the administration had failed to fulfil any of its promises, alleging that the Renewed Hope Agenda had only impoverished Nigerians while enriching government officials.“Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda has only succeeded in impoverishing Nigerians. They have only enriched themselves and that’s all about the hope agenda”, he said.He pointed out that some policies, including the removal of the fuel subsidy, were responsible for the economic hardship bedevilling the masses.“Look at the issue of fuel subsidy, from the very first day Tinubu came into power, he announced that subsidy was gone and that very day, the petroleum pump price jumped up and fuel stations started shutting down. That is where Nigerians’ problems began till today.“There is nothing they have done that gave hope to the ordinary Nigerian. This government failed in security. Every day you keep hearing abuse mass abduction killing and all of that.“They keep saying that they are making progress in security yet we keep seeing more insecurity everyday. The government has done virtually nothing to improve the lives of Nigerians.“You can’t travel by air because of the hike in airfare prices and you can’t move by road because of insecurity. It is a terrible situation that we have been.“Tinubu told us that if he cannot provide electricity, we should not vote for him and we are going to do exactly what he said”, Sampson stated.They want to lie again — Political analystAaron Akogwu, a political analyst and grassroots mobiliser, told DAILY POST that the ruling party has no truth to give.“You can’t give what you don’t have. APC people have no single truth in their mouths. Like 2Baba said in one of his hit songs, it’s like they want to tell us another story again.“The campaign is going to be difficult for them because what are they going to say to the people? The promises you made before we brought you in, have you been able to keep them? Are we expecting a new lie?” he questioned.They only removed fuel, electricity subsidy from the poor and gave to the rich — Isaac FayoseOn his part, Nigerian businessman Prince Isaac Fayose dismissed any improvement in the nation’s economy since Tinubu assumed office, stating that the administration’s policies only favoured the rich.He alleged that the APC government “removed subsidy from fuel and electricity from the poor and gave it to the rich. At a time, I agreed that subsidy must go but I never knew that they would take the subsidy away and replace it with them living large.“The subsidy that was supposed to go to the common man is what they are now using to buy jets, that’s what they are now giving to the governors that are not working.“Despite the subsidy removal, roads to Ekiti, Osun and others are impassable. They are now boasting of cash transfer to the poor. How much is the cash? N5,000 is less than $50. What business can someone do with that?“Go to the North and see how people are suffering. People that spent billions of naira during the Osun election are now boasting of N50,000 cash transfer. Nigerians need to wake up and take their country back”.However, the Finance Minister, Taiwo Oyedele, on Saturday described the latest rating of Nigeria’s economic outlook by Moody’s Ratings, one of the world’s biggest credit rating agencies, as an important external validation of the difficult but necessary reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration.Moody’s, in the rating released on Friday, upgraded Nigeria’s outlook from ‘stable’ to ‘positive’.In a statement made available to journalists, the minister said the Federal Government’s next move was to push Nigeria into what he called investment-grade status.Source: [LINK]

Thread Title: 2027: Obafemi Martins Announces Renewed Hope Tournament For Tinubu’s Campaign

Main Post: Former Super Eagles striker, Obafemi Martins, has announced plans to organise a youth football tournament in support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s 2027 campaign.Martins disclosed this during an interview on TVC on Thursday, saying the tournament, which he described as the “Renewed Hope tournament,” would be held in November.According to the former Inter Milan and Newcastle United striker, the tournament will involve teams from the six geopolitical zones, with additional teams expected to participate.There’s a tournament that I’m doing for His Excellency Bola Ahmed Tinubu that I’m doing for his campaign, the renewal youth tournament, and I’m doing it with, I think, the geopolitical zone, which is six, and I’m adding more two to three teams with it,” Martins said.He said the initiative was aimed not only at supporting Tinubu’s campaign but also at creating opportunities for Nigerian youths.I think I’m just happy to do it for the president with all his hard work and all that. And that is not just for the president, it’s for the Nigerians and the Nigerian youth as well; how we can help them,” he said.Martins said he was funding the tournament himself and confirmed that it would take place in November.“Yes, I’m doing it in November,” he said when asked if the initiative was self-funded.The announcement comes barely two weeks after Martins expressed support for Tinubu’s son, Seyi Tinubu, becoming president of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) in the future.Speaking on the Mikel Obi podcast, Martins had described Seyi as young and someone who understands what Nigerians want.I think Seyi Tinubu can be the president of NFF. He’s young and understands what Nigerians want. He’s not the president yet, but he’s making efforts,” Martins said.Martins’ latest initiative places his youth football activities alongside his expressed support for the Tinubu administration ahead of the 2027 general election.

title: Talata Mafara: ISN Declares National Emergency, Calls For Whole-of-society War O
main_content:
Thread Title: Talata Mafara: ISN Declares National Emergency, Calls For Whole-of-society War O

Main Post: Talata Mafara: ISN Declares National Emergency, Calls for Whole-of-Society War on BanditryLAGOS — The Institute of Security, Nigeria has declared a national emergency over the escalating wave of terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and violent attacks across the country, warning that the imposition of a ₦50 million levy and 100 livestock on residents and traders in Talata Mafara, Zamfara State, represents a serious challenge to the authority of the Nigerian state.The institute described the reported invasion of the Talata Mafara market by non-state actors and the seven-day ultimatum issued to residents as more than ordinary criminality, saying such actions amount to an assault on Nigeria’s sovereignty, economic stability and national cohesion.In a statement issued on Friday and signed by its Deputy President and Chief Executive Officer, Barrister Adebayo Akinade, DFISN, FSCS, PSC, the Institute of Security, Nigeria (ISN) said the situation required an urgent shift from isolated security operations to a coordinated whole-of-government and whole-of-society response.The institute noted that the continued destruction of lives, farms, markets and livelihoods was creating a parallel criminal economy in parts of the country.According to the ISN, the development also raises serious constitutional concerns, particularly with regard to Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, which places the security and welfare of citizens among the primary purposes of government.ISN Demands Coordinated Security FrameworkThe institute called on the Federal and state governments to treat banditry-related levies, attacks on markets and the disruption of legitimate economic activities as matters requiring coordinated security intervention.It urged government to establish a state-led security coordination framework that would bring together federal security agencies, state security outfits and properly vetted community security personnel.The ISN also called for increased funding for tactical mobility, drones, night-vision equipment and aerial surveillance capabilities in frontline states, particularly Zamfara, Katsina, Sokoto, Niger, Kaduna and Plateau.It further recommended the creation of a Special Victims Support and Livelihood Restoration Fund to assist communities affected by terrorism, kidnapping and banditry.Intelligence Must Drive Counter-Banditry OperationsThe security institute said security agencies must move further towards predictive and intelligence-led operations.It called for greater focus on infiltrating criminal networks, particularly the markets and livestock value chains allegedly being exploited to finance and sustain banditry.The institute urged security agencies to dismantle criminal logistics and levy-collection networks while strengthening the regulation of livestock markets.It also advocated a rapid-response framework supported by improved intelligence sharing and aerial surveillance.Citizens, Communities Have Role to PlayThe ISN also urged communities, civil society organisations, traditional institutions, farmers, market associations and religious bodies to establish stronger local early-warning and early-response mechanisms.It recommended the creation of Local Government Area-level Peace and Security Forums to improve information sharing and community engagement.The institute, however, urged citizens to exercise caution and cooperate with security agencies rather than independently confronting armed groups.It called for the documentation and preservation of evidence relating to attacks while encouraging appropriate support for victims of violence.National Security Fusion Centre NeededAs part of its reform proposals, the ISN called for the establishment of a National Security Fusion Centre, supported by state-level fusion desks to facilitate the rapid sharing and analysis of security intelligence.It also advocated the creation of specialised courts or expedited judicial mechanisms for terrorism, banditry and kidnapping cases, subject to constitutional safeguards and due process.Other recommendations included the use of technology for forest monitoring, livestock tracking and citizen reporting, as well as stronger professional regulation and certification within Nigeria's private security sector.The institute said it remained ready to support government, security agencies and communities through research, professional training, policy advisory services and certification in areas including terrorism studies, intelligence management and counter-banditry operations.The ISN stressed that defeating terrorism and banditry would require more than military action, insisting that security, intelligence, community participation, economic recovery and effective justice must work together.Signed:Barr. Adebayo Akinade, DFISN, FSCS, PSCDeputy President & Chief Executive OfficerFor: Institute of Security, Nigeria (ISN)

Thread Title: APC National Chairman Embarks On 2-week Vacation Abroad Outside

Main Post: PRESS STATEMENTOFFICE OF THE NATIONAL CHAIRMAN OF APCAPC National Chairman Takes Two-Week Vacation to Rest, Re-strategise for 2027The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, has commenced a two-week vacation outside of the country following an exceptionally demanding and eventful first year of his tenure as leader of the ruling party.The vacation is a well-deserved period of rest and personal rejuvenation after months of intense party engagements, consultations, travels and strategic activities undertaken by the National Chairman in the course of repositioning and strengthening the APC.Since assuming office, Professor Yilwatda has devoted himself to the task of building a stronger, more cohesive and electorally competitive party, working closely with the National Working Committee (NWC), governors, members of the National Assembly, state party structures, elected officials, stakeholders and millions of party members across the country.Under his leadership, the APC has successfully organised and concluded its National Convention, strengthened its internal structures and successfully conducted its primary elections at the various levels in preparation for the 2027 general elections.These achievements, coming within a relatively short period, have further consolidated the APC's position as Nigeria's leading political party and one of Africa's largest and most formidable political organisations.Far from being a disengagement from party affairs, the vacation provides the National Chairman with an opportunity to step back briefly from the intensity of day-to-day activities, recharge and reflect on the enormous responsibilities ahead.Professor Yilwatda will use the period to rest, retool and further sharpen his strategic thinking ahead of the 2027 general elections, which will be a defining moment for the APC and the Renewed Hope agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.The National Chairman will also utilise the period of respite to reflect on the next phase of the party's development and put finishing touches to the design and planning of the forthcoming National Working Committee Retreat, which is expected to provide an important platform for the NWC to review the party's journey so far, identify emerging challenges and agree on strategies for the months ahead.The retreat is expected to further strengthen coordination within the NWC and enhance the party's preparedness for the demanding electoral season ahead.Professor Yilwatda's decision to take a brief vacation is therefore both timely and necessary, coming after a sustained period of exceptionally rigorous party activities. Leadership, especially at the level of a national political party, requires not only constant engagement but also periods of reflection, strategic assessment and renewal.The APC National Chairman remains fully committed to the party and its objectives. His temporary absence from the country does not in any way affect the operations or functioning of the party, as the National Working Committee continues to discharge its responsibilities in accordance with the party's constitution and established procedures.The National Chairman is expected to return to Nigeria at the end of the two-week vacation and resume his engagements with renewed energy and focus.Signed:Abimbola Tooki Special Adviser to the National ChairmanAll Progressives Congress (APC)(Media and Information Strategy)

title: Peter Obi: Paso Missing As Benue Police Parade 46 Suspects
main_content:
Thread Title: Peter Obi: Paso Missing As Benue Police Parade 46 Suspects

Main Post: The Benue State Police Command has paraded 46 suspects arrested over the blockage of Peter Obi’s convoy in Makurdi on Tuesday, September 8, 2026.Peter Obi, the NDC presidential candidate, had arrived in Benue State to visit the Yelewata community in Guma Local Government Area as part of a humanitarian and condolence visit to survivors and families affected by the deadly June 2025 attack.However, his convoy was stopped along the Makurdi-Gboko federal highway near the airport and Air Force Base by a group of youths who reportedly chanted, “Peter Obi, go back!” Some of the youths were also seen carrying sticks and stones.Following the confrontation, Obi turned back and left the state.The incident sparked controversy after Obi and his supporters alleged that the action was organized by thugs allegedly linked to an aide of Governor Hyacinth Alia, including a Special Adviser on Youth Affairs.The Benue State Government denied any involvement, saying officials were not informed about the visit ahead of time. The government also accused Obi of failing to follow the appropriate protocol and suggested that the incident was being used to create political tension within the NDC.Speaking during a press briefing, Benue State Commissioner of Police, Cletus Nwadiogbu, said the police had been informed of Obi’s visit on Monday evening and had deployed security personnel to ensure his safety.According to the police, a tactical, non-force approach was adopted to prevent the situation from escalating into violence or causing damage to property. Obi was eventually escorted safely back to the airport.The police later launched intelligence-led operations which resulted in the arrest of 46 suspects. The Commissioner said investigations are ongoing and that more suspects, including some key individuals allegedly connected to the incident, are still being sought.The police also stressed that the command remains politically neutral and is committed to protecting the constitutional right to free movement.However, the parade of the 46 suspects has generated fresh reactions online, particularly because some people expected to be among those arrested were not seen in the footage.One name repeatedly mentioned by commenters is Paso Igbe Terzungwe, who some online sources describe as a personal bodyguard of the governor’s Special Adviser on Youth Affairs.Some commenters have questioned why Paso and other alleged organizers or leaders were not visible among the 46 suspects, with some describing the arrests as incomplete and demanding that the police go after those alleged to have organized the blockade.The claims surrounding the missing individuals, however, remain allegations and have not been established as fact by the police.The incident has further intensified political tension surrounding Peter Obi and the Benue State Government, coming against the backdrop of previous disagreements over Obi’s visits to the state and the increasingly heated political atmosphere ahead of the 2027 elections.As the police investigation continues, attention is now shifting to whether more arrests will be made and whether those accused of organizing the blockade will eventually be identified and brought before the public. title: AI Must Strengthen, Not Replace, INEC — Amupitan
main_content:
Thread Title: AI Must Strengthen, Not Replace, INEC — Amupitan

Main Post: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Ojo Amupitan, SAN, has said the successful deployment of Artificial Intelligence, AI, in electoral administration will depend more on strong institutions, governance structures and safeguards than on the sophistication of the technology.Amupitan stated this on Thursday, September 10, 2026, in Ottawa, Canada, while addressing the Global Conference on Responsible AI and Elections, where he presented Nigeria’s experience and lessons in institutionalising responsible AI for electoral administration.He was accompanied by the Director of Information and Communication Technology, ICT, Dr Lawrence Bayode.The INEC chairman said the growing influence of algorithms and data architectures on democratic processes had made responsible technological innovation an important consideration for election management bodies.He said Nigeria had progressively deployed technology to strengthen the credibility and efficiency of its electoral processes, citing the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS; INEC Result Viewing Portal, IReV; and Automated Biometrics Identification System, ABIS, as innovations adopted to reduce human error and manual interference.According to him, the scale of Nigeria’s electoral operations makes technology essential to modern election administration, noting that the country has more than 93 million registered voters, approximately 180,000 polling units and about 185,000 BVAS devices, with elections conducted simultaneously across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.He, however, cautioned that AI adoption should not be driven by technology for its own sake, but by demonstrable improvements in electoral administration, public service and public confidence.“AI must strengthen electoral integrity, improve public service, and always remain under human control,” Amupitan said.He also outlined the legal framework underpinning the deployment of technology in Nigeria’s electoral process, citing the Constitution, Electoral Act 2026, INEC Regulations, Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and Cybercrimes Act 2024.He particularly highlighted provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 relating to the voters’ register, electronic voting devices, biometric accreditation, electronic transmission of results and the use of accreditation and transmitted results in the collation and declaration of election results.The INEC chairman disclosed that the Commission had commenced institutional preparations for the responsible adoption of AI, rather than treating it solely as an ICT project.He said the Commission had established a dedicated Artificial Intelligence Division within its ICT Department, developed an AI Roadmap for phased adoption and an AI Governance Framework currently undergoing internal approval.He added that INEC had commenced AI literacy and technical capacity building among staff, while adopting a multidisciplinary approach involving ICT, Operations, Legal, Voter Education, Risk Management and other departments.“Responsible AI begins with institutional readiness — not technology,” he said.Amupitan identified five principles guiding INEC’s AI initiatives as human oversight; transparency and accountability; data protection and privacy; cybersecurity and risk management; and operational value and public trust.He stressed that AI would serve as an aid to election officials and would not replace human responsibility for electoral decision-making.Giving an insight into one of the Commission’s AI initiatives, Amupitan disclosed that INEC had introduced an intelligent Results Management process designed to assist in identifying discrepancies in election result records.[LINK]

title: Yayi, Ogun West And The Politics Of Readiness - Adeolu Adebari
main_content:
Thread Title: Yayi, Ogun West And The Politics Of Readiness - Adeolu Adebari

Main Post: Every election season, the same scenario plays out in Ogun State. Family history is questioned. Home ownership is scrutinised. Senate districts become battlegrounds of identity. The 2027 gubernatorial election follows this pattern, with Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola’s long tenure in Lagos cited by his opponents as a weakness in his Ogun identity.However, a state with Ogun’s potential deserves better than a rehash of old squabbles. The most important questions voters are asking are neither new nor complex. Who can govern from day one? Who understands the strain on public finances, the urgent need for infrastructure, the pressure on employment, the need for schools, and the everyday struggles of ordinary families? These are the issues that should define 2027, not family house politics. Ogun doesn’t need a governor based on family lineage. It needs a governor based on competence.In our politics, lineage is invoked far too often when performance analysis is difficult. When a person’s career path is minimal, people exaggerate their origins. When their influence is visible, the conversation shifts from devotion to genealogy. Identity mobilises the masses, but it doesn’t build roads, create jobs, or strengthen the institutions we need. This is the poverty of identity politics, as it merely generates enthusiasm at campaign rallies and leaves the state exactly where it found it. Or make it worse.However, Adeola’s origins are undeniable. His paternal roots trace back to Ago-Isaga and Pahayi in Ilaro, while his maternal lineage links him to Kemta in Egbaland. Traditional leaders, temporal and spiritual authorities, merchants, and other key players in Yewa and Egbaland have recognised him as omo oye, a legitimate son of the region’s cultural and political heritage. If the guardians of that heritage have spoken so clearly, then it is just and sensible that the entire state of Ogun accept him as one of their own. He should not be treated as an outsider seeking borrowed legitimacy, but as a leader whose identity the communities to which he belongs have validated.More pressing issues lie elsewhere. Should a strategic state like Ogun sacrifice its future in a debate that cannot guarantee the livelihoods of its people or repair a single road? Its farmers need better roads to transport their crops, storage facilities, and credit to increase yields. Its traders need stronger markets and security. Its youth need more jobs, training, and greater opportunities. Its communities need water, electricity, schools, and truly functional primary healthcare. Its industrial corridors need infrastructure that matches the investment. None of these challenges will be solved by arguing over district names.Governing is not for amateurs. The responsibilities of the executive office are too weighty to rely on sentimentality, improvisation, or trial and error. A governor must understand budgetary language, respect institutional discipline, master the politics of negotiation, and have the patience to translate priorities into measurable results.Adeola has come a long way in public service. From the Lagos State House of Representatives, where he served from 2003 to 2011 and chaired the Finance Committee, to the House of Representatives, where he chaired the Public Accountability Committee, and then to the Senate, first for Lagos West and since 2023 for Ogun West. His career has been a continuous learning experience in legislation, oversight, district management, and the complex relationship between politics and public finance. As a certified public accountant and current chair of the Senate Budget Committee, he sits at the heart of the national budget, where the numbers must add up, competing demands for public funds must be considered, and fiscal priorities must be championed beyond mere rhetoric. The fact that he comes to these responsibilities with a technical background in accounting further strengthens the argument that he brings substance to a field often saturated with noise.Ogun is too strategic a state to be learnt on the job. It’s an industrial, border state, a manufacturing corridor, and a neighbour of Lagos. The next governor must understand money, policy, negotiation, and implementation, and shouldn’t spend their first few years learning the fundamentals of governance. The state needs a leader who can meet with technocrats, engage development partners, evaluate public procurement options, interpret the budget beyond its formal presentation, and take projects from promise to document and from document to construction. Adeola’s greatest appeal lies precisely in this, as he appears ready to take office in Oke-Mosan with a practical understanding of the system.Politics only has meaning when it impacts people’s lives. In almost all communities of Ogun State, Adeola’s interventions have achieved precisely that. Roads have been built and rehabilitated. Access to rural areas has improved. Solar-powered streetlights have extended commercial activity and community life well past nightfall. These small but tangible improvements are how ordinary citizens assess whether the government is truly present.Their empowerment programmes have benefited women, artisans, young entrepreneurs, and small business owners. In times of economic hardship, this kind of support is not a luxury. A grant, a sewing machine, business equipment, or a new skill can mean the difference between dependency and dignity for an entire family. The Oloja Yayi Market Support Fund has become a symbol of this approach. Nigeria’s informal economy bears the brunt of daily life’s hardships, and support for vendors quickly translates into school tuition, job training, food, and necessities.It’s easy to overlook these interventions in elite conversations, but those who understand the social economy of our communities know this well.Education is not neglected either. Classrooms, ICT support, and scholarships reflect the state’s future. Ogun cannot continue to project itself as an industrial destination if it neglects the human resources that must drive those ambitions, as factories need workers, technology needs skilled minds, and development needs an educated citizenry. Healthcare, water, and electricity are also part of his interventions in primary healthcare centres, drinking water systems, transformers, thus ensuring that public services are not luxuries, but they essential for daily survival. Governance is most meaningful when it solves everyday problems.Critics who focus on the sheer number of these projects miss the fundamental message. Their true value lies in their vision and scope: policy should impact lives, open doors, and improve communities. Equally important, their dissemination beyond a narrow base reinforces the argument that Adeola’s gubernatorial aspirations are comprehensive in conception, not sectoral in design.It has become fashionable to pretend that access is unimportant in Nigeria’s federal system. In fact, access is crucial. States do not develop in isolation but thrive through a clear vision, quality leadership, and the ability to negotiate with the central government without sacrificing local priorities. Any governor who understands the mechanisms of national power has a distinct advantage in attracting attention, resources, and strategic alliances.Adeola’s role in the Senate budget process places him at the intersection of national priorities and public spending. Properly leveraged for Ogun, this proximity could further accelerate the rehabilitation and expansion of key federal highways traversing the state, strengthen the need for rail and industrial port connections, and capitalise on federal trade policy and special economic zone incentives to attract manufacturing hubs and logistics investment. This could further help channel federal agricultural interventions, climate resilience funding, and digital economy initiatives directly to Ogun’s rural and urban communities.Lest anyone misunderstand, this is not a call for Ogun to become dependent on Abuja. Rather, it calls for leadership that knows how to secure the state’s share while strengthening its own economy. A governor who understands the seat of government can negotiate more effectively, attract more investment, and achieve results more quickly. And Ogun’s location makes this ability even more crucial: the state shares Lagos’s economic dynamism, serves as an industrial gateway to Nigeria, and has enormous potential in manufacturing, agriculture, logistics, and entrepreneurship. But geography is only an advantage in the hands of leadership that knows how to use it, a leadership that can engage with investors, negotiate with Abuja, and, at the same time, understand rural roads, market stalls, and public schools. In this, Adeola is uniquely positioned as the most able of all contestants to expand the successes of the Governor Dapo Abiodun administration.The issue of Ogun West Senatorial District remains one of the most unresolved matters in the state’s political history. Since 1976, Ogun East and Ogun Central have produced governors multiple times, while Ogun West has been waiting. This fact carries real moral and political weight as it speaks to inclusion, balance, and the need for every part of the state to feel empowered in the highest office.However, equality should not be reduced to mere sentimentality, and the governorship is too important to be granted simply as compensation. Ogun West’s strongest argument in 2027 will not be based solely on grievances, but on the quality of the candidate it presents. In Adeola, the region offers a man who can argue from experience and equality, grounded in commitment and preparation.The 2027 elections will test Ogun’s political maturity. The state can waste another season arguing over trivial matters, or it can confront the real question before it: who has the preparation, scope, experience, and discipline necessary to propel Ogun’s progress?Adeola isn’t perfect. No candidate is. But politics isn’t a search for angels but a choice between people with verifiable track records. In that sense, his experience is tangible, his networks are valuable, his knowledge of public finances is proven, and his connection to grassroots politics is evident. His opponents are free to refute these claims, as is appropriate in a democracy. But Ogun’s voters must insist that these arguments transcend rumours.Ogun State doesn’t need a merely ceremonial governor in 2027. It needs a builder, someone with the confidence to negotiate, the discipline to manage resources, and the courage to bring development to every district. The state must look beyond appearances and prioritise substance. Each candidate must be judged on their preparation, competence, temperament, vision, and ability to execute. By these criteria, Yayi has presented Ogun State with a case it cannot wish away.Adeolu Adebari, the Managing Partner, Constellation Holdings, writes from Itoko, Abeokuta, Ogun State[LINK]

title: ‘Who Says Hunye Is Irrelevant?’ Massive Crowd at Tinubu Rally Signals Rising
main_content:
Thread Title: ‘Who Says Hunye Is Irrelevant?’ Massive Crowd at Tinubu Rally Signals Rising

Main Post: ‘Who Says Hunye Is Irrelevant?’ Massive Crowd at Tinubu Rally Signals Rising Political Clout (VIDEO)- Says Nigeria Is Moving Forward, Urges Ogun Voters to Support APCABEOKUTA — The growing political profile of All Progressives Congress governorship aspirant in Ogun State, Hon. Abayomi Hunye, came under renewed focus on Thursday as he joined the Coalition of Registered Political Parties (CRPP) to mobilise support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid.The rally, held at the Ake Palace axis of Abeokuta, attracted a large crowd and provided a fresh indication of Hunye’s ability to mobilise supporters and command attention in the Ogun political space.The turnout has also sparked fresh conversations among political observers about the relevance and grassroots reach of the governorship aspirant, particularly against recent claims in some quarters that he lacks sufficient political influence to shape events in the state.For his supporters, the gathering offered a direct response to such claims: that a politician described as having little or no political clout would struggle to mobilise a significant crowd in the state capital for a major political event.Speaking at the rally, Hunye praised President Tinubu’s administration, particularly its infrastructure projects and economic reforms, and urged Nigerians to support the President’s re-election in 2027.The APC governorship aspirant said the Tinubu administration had recorded visible achievements since assuming office, expressing optimism that the country would continue to witness development if Nigerians supported the President.According to Hunye, “The President has been able to take Nigeria out of where it used to be, with many visible achievements recorded during his first term.”He also compared Tinubu’s leadership approach, particularly in education, with that of the late Premier of the Western Region, Chief Obafemi Awolowo.Hunye urged residents of Ogun State to support the APC and its candidates in the 2027 general elections, saying continued support for the party would help consolidate development and democratic dividends in the state.“Ogun State will be better. Let us vote for all APC candidates in 2027 so that Nigeria will continue to experience development and democratic dividends,” he said.“If Tinubu returns for a second term, we will all enjoy his government. Let us re-elect Tinubu for the betterment of the future of our nation.”Hunye also dismissed what he described as negative narratives about the direction of the state, urging residents not to be misled by claims that Ogun was moving backwards.“Don’t listen to those who are saying we are moving back. They are not saying the truth. We are not moving back; we are moving forward for the betterment of our state,” he said.The rally was organised by the CRPP in support of Tinubu’s administration and his proposed 2027 re-election bid.Chairman of the CRPP in Ogun, Olaposi Oginni, reaffirmed the coalition’s support for the President and said the group was at the rally to appreciate Tinubu’s efforts in infrastructure and economic reforms.“We are here to support Mr President and appreciate his efforts. There is no alternative to making the right choice at the polls in 2027,” Oginni said.He also urged Nigerians to support the administration’s economic reforms, describing the ongoing efforts to reposition the economy as a recovery process that should be sustained.Beyond the immediate purpose of the rally, however, Hunye’s visibility at the event and the turnout recorded have added a new dimension to the political conversation in Ogun ahead of the 2027 governorship contest.With the race expected to intensify in the coming months, Thursday’s mobilisation could further fuel debate over the aspirant’s grassroots network, political reach and ability to influence the unfolding contest within the Ogun APC. Electricity transmission along the Kainji-Birnin Kebbi corridor has been disrupted after strong winds and heavy rainfall reportedly caused the collapse of a major transmission tower. The Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) confirmed the incident in a statement issued on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, saying the damage affected the 330kV Kainji-Birnin Kebbi transmission line. The company subsequently declared force majeure on the affected line, citing the natural disaster responsible for the damage. Transmission Line Trips Twice According to TCN, the affected line, identified as 2KNJ-BRK1, tripped at about 10:44pm on Monday, September 7. An attempt was made to restore the line at approximately 11:07pm, but the line tripped again. Following the second incident, TCN deployed linesmen from its Birnin Kebbi Sub-Region to inspect the transmission corridor and establish the cause of the fault. The inspection team later discovered that Tower T367 had collapsed. > “Preliminary findings indicate that the collapse of the tower was caused by heavy winds and rainstorms experienced in the area,” TCN said. TCN Begins Restoration Efforts The collapsed tower has disrupted the transmission of bulk electricity through the 330kV Kainji-Birnin Kebbi corridor. TCN said it had commenced arrangements to move personnel, equipment and other required materials to the affected location for the reconstruction of the tower. The company said the exercise is aimed at restoring normal bulk electricity transmission along the corridor as quickly as possible. Alternative Route Maintains Power Supply Despite the damage to the transmission line, TCN said it had been able to maintain electricity transmission to Sokoto through an alternative route. According to the company, the Talata Mafara-Sokoto corridor was receiving electricity through another transmission route from the Kaduna-Mando axis. The alternative arrangement utilises the 132kV Zaria-Funtua-Gusau transmission line, helping to maintain power supply to affected areas while restoration plans are being implemented. TCN Apologises to Consumers TCN apologised to electricity consumers and other stakeholders for the disruption caused by the incident. The company assured the public that it was taking steps to restore normal bulk electricity transmission on the affected Kainji-Birnin Kebbi corridor as soon as possible. Access Premium News[LINK]

title: The Fight For Democracy: Hang Abiola, Ojukwu Tells Abacha ��
main_content:
Thread Title: The Fight For Democracy: Hang Abiola, Ojukwu Tells Abacha ��

Main Post: HANG ABIOLA, OJUKWU TELLS ABACHA 🇳🇬LAGOS, 1994: The history of Nigeria's political crisis took another dramatic turn when Chief Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu, the former leader of Biafra, publicly advised General Sani Abacha to deal decisively with Chief M.K.O. Abiola.Speaking in Kaduna at the launch of Nigeria: The State of the Nation and Windfall, published by Arewa House, Ojukwu accused Abiola of treason, alleging that he invited foreign sanctions against Nigeria and declared himself President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces. He dismissed June 12 as “an apparition” and called on Abacha to deal with Abiola, effectively seeking the death penalty. He reportedly said: “June 12 is not real; there is nothing like it.”But Ojukwu's own history makes those words even more difficult to forget.When Biafra was collapsing in January 1970, Ojukwu took all the foreign currency in the Bank of Biafra, left his people, and fled into exile in Côte d'Ivoire, where he was enjoying life with young girls. To his critics, it was the act of a coward who abandoned his people when the war he had led was finally lost. While ordinary Biafrans were left to face the consequences of the war, Ojukwu was thousands of miles away.For about twelve years, he remained in exile.Then President Shehu Shagari granted him a pardon in 1982, and Ojukwu returned to Nigeria after all he had looted was finished.But the political reversal was extraordinary.The former Biafran leader later entered Nigerian politics, joining the National Party of Nigeria (NPN), a party strongly associated with Northern political power. This was the same Ojukwu who had once presented himself as a defender of his people against the Northern establishment. In 1983, he contested the Senate election in Onitsha under the NPN and lost.Now compare that journey with M.K.O. Abiola.Abiola didn't lead his people to a war. He was a businessman and politician who entered the democratic process, won the June 12, 1993, presidential election according to the widely held historical view, and became the symbol of a struggle for the restoration of democratic government.When the election was annulled, Abiola refused to disappear. He came home and stood up. He demanded his mandate.He knew the military could arrest him. He knew his wealth could not save him. He knew the consequences could be devastating.Still, he stayed.His struggle helped make June 12 a lasting symbol of Nigeria's democratic aspirations and contributed to the political memory behind the democracy Nigerians enjoy today.When Abacha arrested him in 1994, Abiola remained in detention rather than surrender the mandate he believed belonged to the Nigerian people.And while this man was behind bars, Ojukwu was publicly telling Abacha to hang him. That contrast remains one of the most painful ironies of Nigerian history.Ojukwu left when Biafra was collapsing and later returned through a presidential pardon.Abiola stayed when his democratic struggle became dangerous.Ojukwu became a shadow of his former political self.Abiola became a martyr of Nigeria's democratic struggle.One ran into exile when his war was lost. The other stayed home when his democracy was taken away.One fought with guns.The other fought with his voice, his political mandate, and his refusal to surrender.And today, Nigerians enjoy a democratic government while remembering June 12 and the sacrifices of people like M.K.O. Abiola.He came home. He stood his ground. He refused to surrender. And he paid the ultimate price.#Ojukwu #MKOAbiola #June12 #SaniAbacha #Biafra #NigeriaHistory #NigerianHistory #Democracy #PoliticalHistory 🇳🇬Now follow the link below to watch mko's last interview and also listen to MKO Abiola last speech as he was being arrested and takem away by the military [LINK]

While ordinary Biafrans were left to face the consequences of the war, Ojukwu was thousands of miles away.For about twelve years, he remained in exile.Then President Shehu Shagari granted him a pardon in 1982, and Ojukwu returned to Nigeria after all he had looted was finished.But the political reversal was extraordinary.The former Biafran leader later entered Nigerian politics, joining the National Party of Nigeria (NPN), a party strongly associated with Northern political power. This was the same Ojukwu who had once presented himself as a defender of his people against the Northern establishment. In 1983, he contested the Senate election in Onitsha under the NPN and lost.Now compare that journey with M.K.O. Abiola.Abiola didn't lead his people to a war. He was a businessman and politician who entered the democratic process, won the June 12, 1993, presidential election according to the widely held historical view, and became the symbol of a struggle for the restoration of democratic government.When the election was annulled, Abiola refused to disappear. He came home and stood up. He demanded his mandate.He knew the military could arrest him. He knew his wealth could not save him. He knew the consequences could be devastating.Still, he stayed.His struggle helped make June 12 a lasting symbol of Nigeria's democratic aspirations and contributed to the political memory behind the democracy Nigerians enjoy today.When Abacha arrested him in 1994, Abiola remained in detention rather than surrender the mandate he believed belonged to the Nigerian people.And while this man was behind bars, Ojukwu was publicly telling Abacha to hang him. That contrast remains one of the most painful ironies of Nigerian history.Ojukwu left when Biafra was collapsing and later returned through a presidential pardon.Abiola stayed when his democratic struggle became dangerous.Ojukwu became a shadow of his former political self.Abiola became a martyr of Nigeria's democratic struggle.One ran into exile when his war was lost. The other stayed home when his democracy was taken away.One fought with guns.The other fought with his voice, his political mandate, and his refusal to surrender.And today, Nigerians enjoy a democratic government while remembering June 12 and the sacrifices of people like M.K.O. Abiola.He came home. He stood his ground. He refused to surrender. And he paid the ultimate price.#Ojukwu #MKOAbiola #June12 #SaniAbacha #Biafra #NigeriaHistory #NigerianHistory #Democracy #PoliticalHistory 🇳🇬Now follow the link below to watch mko's last interview and also listen to MKO Abiola last speech as he was being arrested and takem away by the military [LINK] have quoted more than you posted. title: 2027 Election: Economic Hardship, Northern Politics And Police Accountability
main_content:
Thread Title: 2027 Election: Economic Hardship, Northern Politics And Police Accountability

Main Post: Nigeria is moving towards another important election in 2027. Political alliances are already taking shape.At the same time, Nigerians are dealing with economic hardship, insecurity and rising living costs. These issues could have a major impact on the next election.A recent political discussion examined several important issues. They included economic reforms, Northern politics, the Middle Belt, political alliances and police accountability.Economic policies could influence the 2027 electionGovernment policies can change people's lives in significant ways.Some economic reforms may improve the country's long-term prospects. However, they can also create difficulties for households in the short term.Many Nigerians are currently concerned about food prices, transportation costs, electricity bills and other daily expenses.This raises an important question. Will the government's economic policies improve people's lives before the 2027 election?Economic performance could become one of the biggest factors influencing voters.Political leaders may therefore need to focus more on practical economic solutions than political arguments.The Middle Belt and Northern politicsThe political relationship between the Middle Belt and the wider North has a long history.Religion, ethnicity and regional interests have influenced political relationships for decades.The Middle Belt also developed its own political identity. Many communities in the region have different historical and cultural experiences from those associated with the traditional Northern political establishment.However, the politics of the region cannot be explained by religion alone.Political alliances have also been influenced by economic interests, access to power and the search for regional representation.Awolowo and the politics of the First RepublicThe discussion also examined the role of Chief Obafemi Awolowo in Nigeria's First Republic politics.Awolowo's political movement sought support beyond the Western Region. His political strategy included relationships with groups in other parts of the country.However, political competition created disagreements between Awolowo's movement and the Northern People's Congress.These disagreements reflected differences in political ideology, regional interests and competition for power.Nigeria's political history shows that alliances can change when political circumstances change.Kwankwaso, Atiku and the Northern voteThe relationship between Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso and Atiku Abubakar also featured prominently in the discussion.Both politicians have strong political bases in Northern Nigeria.During the 2023 presidential election, the Northern vote was divided between different political candidates.Atiku maintained significant support in several Northern states. Kwankwaso also attracted strong support, particularly in Kano and parts of the North.This division affected the overall electoral calculations.The question now is whether Northern political forces will remain divided ahead of 2027.Will the economy influence 2027?Economic hardship could change the way Nigerians vote.Many voters are concerned about the cost of living. They also want better employment opportunities, improved security and more affordable basic services.If economic conditions improve, the government could benefit politically.However, if hardship continues, voters may become more critical of the government.Economic concerns could also reduce the influence of traditional political loyalties.Religion and ethnicity still matterReligion and ethnicity remain important factors in Nigerian politics.However, they are not the only factors that determine how people vote.Voters also consider the economy, security, leadership and personal welfare.Younger voters, in particular, may place greater emphasis on economic opportunities and good governance.This could make the 2027 election more competitive.Nigerians and police accountabilityThe discussion also focused on whether Nigerians should be allowed to record police officers while they are performing their duties.Some Nigerians believe citizens should be able to document police activities in public places.They argue that recordings can provide evidence when misconduct occurs.Recordings can also protect police officers against false allegations.The issue is therefore not simply about recording police officers. It is about transparency and accountability.Who should watch the police?Police authorities use surveillance cameras and other technologies to monitor public spaces.This raises an important question.If authorities can monitor citizens, should citizens also be able to document the conduct of public officers?Supporters of citizen recordings say transparency should work both ways.Police officers are public officials. They are expected to protect lives and property.When they perform their duties in public, independent recordings can provide useful evidence. READ MORE [LINK]

title: Ogun Releases N6.75bn For Gratuity, Additional Pension Benefits
main_content:
Thread Title: Ogun Releases N6.75bn For Gratuity, Additional Pension Benefits

Main Post: The Ogun State Government has released N6.75 billion for the payment of gratuity and Additional Pension Benefits (APB) to retirees in the state.The Head of Service, Mr. Olanrewaju Saka, mni, disclosed this in a statement on Friday, saying the release was part of the government’s continued efforts to address outstanding pension obligations and improve the welfare of retired workers.According to him, N2.751 billion was released to pay gratuity to 432 beneficiaries, while another N4 billion was released for the payment of Additional Pension Benefits to eligible retirees from July 2025 to date.Saka said the government remained committed to ensuring that workers who had served the state meritoriously received their retirement benefits, despite competing demands on the state’s resources.Explaining the Additional Pension Benefit, Saka said it was introduced to cushion the difference between the pension benefits retirees would have received under the old Defined Benefit Scheme (DBS) and what they are entitled to under the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS).He explained that while workers under the CPS have retirement savings in their Retirement Savings Accounts, some retirees could receive lower benefits than they would have been entitled to under the former scheme. The APB, therefore, provides an additional payment from the state government to eligible retirees to bridge part of that gap.Saka stressed that the APB is separate from the funds in retirees’ Retirement Savings Accounts and does not reduce the savings accumulated in those accounts.He said the latest release demonstrated the administration’s commitment to providing greater financial security and dignity for retirees, adding that the government would continue to address outstanding pension and gratuity obligations in a systematic and sustainable manner.The Head of Service assured retirees that the government would maintain transparency and engagement in the administration of retirement benefits, while urging serving public officers to ensure that their pension records and documentation were accurate and up to date.He reaffirmed the commitment of the Prince Dapo Abiodun administration to building a pension system that would enable public servants to approach retirement with greater confidence and security.

title: Tinubu's Wife Launches National Food Bank, Empowers 5000 Women In Anambra,
main_content:
Thread Title: Tinubu's Wife Launches National Food Bank, Empowers 5000 Women In Anambra,

Main Post: Tinubu's Wife launches National Food Bank, empowers 5,000 women in AnambraBy OGEMDI OZOEMENAM, AwkaThe First Lady of Nigeria and wife of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Senator Oluremi Tinubu has launched the National Community Food Bank Programme (NCFBP) in Anambra State, which concluded the launch of the programme in the five states of the South-East geopolitical zone.While the Food Bank was launched at old Governor's Lodge Amawbia, she inaugurated the Tertiary Education Trust Fund-sponsored ICT Experience Centre at the Federal Polytechnic, Oko.The programme climaxed on Thursday at Dr Alex Ekwueme Square Awka in the presence of traditional rulers, APGA and APC supporters, wives of Bauchi, Imo, Ebonyi, Abia and Kebbi states, Ministers and Anambra LGAs chairmen.The First Lady said the programme was designed to support women and children and enhance their livelihoods in the state and other parts of the South-East.She empowered more than 500 women drawn from the 21 local government areas and three senatorial districts of Anambra State with N100,000 each, stressing that the launch of the NCFBP had brought Renewed Hope to Nigerian women and children.Oluremi disclosed that N100,000 would be donated to each of the beneficiaries, amounting to N500 million, to support them, in addition to other empowerment items such as sewing machines, farm seedlings, pigs, goats and other materials.Mrs Tinubu also flagged off the statewide empowerment programme of the wife of the Anambra State Governor, Dr Nonye Soludo, with 5,000 beneficiaries across the state’s 21 local government areas receiving business grants, vocational tools and equipment for agriculture and agro-processing, beauty care and small-scale enterprises.Senator Oluremi said she was in Anambra State and other states in the South-East not for political campaigns but as a Nigerian to foster unity among Nigerians and support citizens, regardless of their political affiliations or geographical locations.While maintaining that she would return to the region for campaign when the time comes, Mrs Tinubu urged Nigerians to strive to see every citizen as a brother and sister, regardless of where they live across the country.Governor Chukwuma Soludo applauded President Bola Tinubu’s macroeconomic and infrastructural reforms, declaring that the administration’s policies are actively working to steer the nation toward recovery.While welcoming the First Lady to the “Light of the Nation,” Governor described her as a loving mother, supportive wife, and compassionate leader whose public service exemplifies true philanthropy and biblical values.He noted that the national economy is in dire need of resuscitation when President Tinubu assumed office, expressing firm confidence that the next four years of the current administration will birth a stronger and fairer Nigeria.While highlighting cross-party synergy, Governor Soludo noted that progressives must work together for the nation’s progress, pointing to the collaborative alliance between the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA)—which he termed synonymous with Anambra—and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).The Governor outlined plans to continue to cascade federal initiatives down to local communities and announced that the National Community Food Bank Programme would be expanded to every community, ensuring that every Primary Health Centre (PHC) hosts a food bank.The highpoint of the occasion was the conferment of a Chieftaincy title “Ugoeze Anambra (meaning the King's Glory Anambra) on President Tinubu's wife, Senator Oluremi by the Chairman Anambra State Traditional Rulers Council and traditional rulers of Obosi, Igwe Chidubem Iweka.###

I am contesting.”Instead, we got corporations, CEOs, shareholders, institutions and party processes. The passengers followed the driver.So when the question suddenly becomes whether Peter Obi can surrender Peter Obi’s presidential ticket, the CEO discovers the shareholders.Obi’s recent appearance around Seyi Makinde only makes clarity more important. It proves no secret deal, but in an atmosphere already filled with speculation about opposition realignments, ambiguity is terrible messaging.If Obi is definitely contesting, say so. If the ticket remains negotiable, say that too.But by September 2026, the candidate should not still sound like an aspirant.OJY OKPE GAVE PETER OBI A CHANCE TO CLOSE THE DOOR. HE LEFT IT AJAR.

title: Why Atiku Still Believes He Can Lead Nigeria Despite Past Disappointments
main_content:
Thread Title: Why Atiku Still Believes He Can Lead Nigeria Despite Past Disappointments

Main Post: Few politicians in Nigeria’s democratic history have pursued the presidency as persistently as Atiku Abubakar.The former vice president has spent decades seeking the country’s highest office. Despite several unsuccessful attempts, he remains in the race and has repeatedly argued that he still has something to offer Nigeria. His determination has earned both admiration and criticism.Supporters describe him as experienced and resilient.Critics argue that Nigerians have heard his promises before.So why does Atiku keep coming back?He believes experience mattersAtiku has consistently argued that his years in government and business make him qualified to lead Nigeria.In recent interviews, he said leadership requires experience and that his next presidential bid would likely be his final attempt. To supporters, that experience is an asset.To critics, it is evidence that Nigeria may need a new generation of leaders.He believes Nigeria’s problems remain unsolvedAtiku has frequently pointed to economic hardship, insecurity and governance challenges as reasons for remaining active in politics.His campaign message continues to focus on economic reforms, job creation and national unity. Whether voters agree with his solutions is a different question.The presidency remains unfinished businessMany political observers believe Atiku sees the presidency as the one major goal missing from his long political career.After serving as vice president between 1999 and 2007, reaching the presidency would complete a political journey that has lasted decades.Does Nigeria still want him?This is where opinions become divided.Some Nigerians see him as a familiar figure with extensive experience.Others believe the country should move beyond politicians who have dominated the political scene for years.The challenge for Atiku is convincing voters that a leader who has been part of Nigeria’s political establishment for decades can still represent change.The bigger questionThe debate may not really be about Atiku.It may be about what Nigerians want from their leaders.Do voters prefer experience?Do they want younger faces?Do they want political outsiders?Or do they simply want whoever can improve their lives?Those questions will likely shape the 2027 election more than any single candidate.Only Atiku knows his true intentions.Some see a politician driven by a genuine belief that he can improve Nigeria.Others see a veteran politician unwilling to let go of a lifelong ambition.What is certain is that, despite multiple defeats, he remains convinced that he still has a path to the presidency. Whether Nigerians agree will ultimately be decided at the ballot box. Source: [LINK]

Main Post: Anambra doctors call off strike after 13 monthsFebruary 28, 2012After over a year of down tools, Anambra State Government employed medical doctors have finally called of strike.According to Dr. Emma Ekwesianya, Chairman Anambra State chapter of Nigeria Medical Association (NMA), the striking doctors decided to pick up tools again because of the plight of the ordinary people in the societ. “It is true, we have called off the strike. We have just signed the agreement with government about an hour ago. The Secretary to the State Government (SSG) signed for the government. A technical committee, headed by Prof. O.O. Mbonu was set up to execute the agreement.” He confirmed.“We decided to take the 60 per cent offered by government because of our people. Government has been rigid and we do not want to continue with the rigidity of government. We are serving the people, not government and our people are suffering.”Speaking further, Ekwesianya, revealed that a technical committee, headed by Prof. O.O. Mbonu had also been set up by the association to see to the implementation of the agreement with government sequel to the signing of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Peter Obi-led government on Monday.Chief Medical Director, Anambra State University Teaching Hospital (ASUTH), Amaku, Awka, Dr. Lawrence Ikeakor also confirmed the new development: “Well I’m happy to tell you that the strike has been amicably resolved, even though, like you said, it’s been a prolonged one but suffice it to say that it has been resolved and the doctors have resumed work.”“The call off was yesterday (Sunday). The doctors had some negotiations and held their congress yesterday, during which they agreed to call off the strike. So they resumed duty today.They are in their clinic. Well, I was not privy to the agreement but I will say that our representatives were satisfied with the arrangement, hence they decided to call off the strike.” He disclosed.[LINK]

Anambra state is the single-highest shareholder in that facility. I invested in it, over $20 million,” Obi had said.“It is worth almost $100 [million] today. That’s what government should do.”TheCable had previously fact-checked some of the claims.Chukwuma Soludo, governor of Anambra, also debunked a recent statement ascribed to him regarding the investment.International Breweries (IB) Plc is a subsidiary of the world’s largest brewer, Anheuser-Busch InBev (AB InBev) — a multinational drink and brewing giant based in Leuven, Belgium.In its 2021 audited financial statement, the company said it holds 43 percent economic interest in International Breweries Plc, a publicly listed company in Nigeria.According to a report by The Nation, AB InBev merged its Nigerian operations under a single corporate entity in 2017. It had three indirect Nigerian subsidiaries — International Breweries Plc, Intafact Beverages Limited and Pabod Breweries Limited. SABMiller Nigeria Holdings BV — another subsidiary of AB InBev — was also a major stakeholder in Intafact and Pabod.ANAMBRA’S INVESTMENTIn a statement made available to TheCable on Tuesday, Ifeatu Onejeme, Anambra’s commissioner of finance, confirmed that Peter Obi’s administration invested the sum of N1,955,535,247.00 (an equivalent of approximately $12,616,356.43 at the then average CBN exchange rate of N155.00/$1) in Intafact Beverages Limited, a green-field brewery set up in Onitsha by SABMiller Breweries of South Africa in 2012.Onejeme added that the state government still holds 407,321,264 ordinary shares of International Breweries Plc in exchange for the Intafact Beverages Limited investment.“Based on the NGX closing price of N5.50 as of 20/6/22, these shares were valued at N2,240,266,952 on that date,” the statement reads in part.“Based on the Central Bank of Nigeria I&E exchange rate of N415.75/US$1.00 on same June 20, 2022, this investment was valued at an equivalent of approximately US$5,388,495.37 (and at N604/$1.00 parallel market rate, only US$3,709,051.24).”[LINK]
