OCTOBER 4, 2021Report: How Peter Obi as Anambra governor failed to declare assets kept in tax havensPeter Obi, former governor of Anambra state, kept secret assets in tax havens, a series of leaked documents has shown.The leaked files which were retrieved from 14 offshore services firms around the world were revealed in a Pandora Papers project led by the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ), and which Premium Times is a part of.In his response, the former governor told Premium Times: “I don’t declare what is owned with others. If my family owns something I won’t declare it. I didn’t declare anything I jointly owed with anyone.” In 2010, more than four years after Obi became governor, he reportedly set up his first discreet company in the British Virgin Island, and named the company Gabriella Investments Limited, after his daughter. To set up what has now become a convoluted business structure, Obi, Premium Times reported first approached Acces International, a secrecy enabler in Monaco, France, to help him incorporate an offshore entity in one of the world’s most notorious tax havens noted for providing conduits for wealthy and privileged corrupt political elites to hide stolen cash. According to the newspaper, Obi also paid Acces International to provide nominee directors for the company — these directors are residents of tax havens paid to sit on boards of companies to hide the identities of real owners of offshore firms.Acces International officials, who reportedly took briefs from Obi and or his representatives, headed to the British Virgin Island where they contracted a local registered agent – Aleman Cordero Galindo & Lee Trust (BVI) Limited (Alcogal) — to set up Gabriella Investments Limited for the former governor.[LINK]

title: What Should A Delta Governor Actually Be Judged By?
main_content:
Thread Title: What Should A Delta Governor Actually Be Judged By?

Main Post: Every election season, we hear promises.New projects.New programmes.New announcements.But after the campaign posters come down, the real question remains:What changed in the lives of ordinary Deltans?A governor should not be judged by how many speeches were delivered or how impressive government announcements sounded.Judge the government by whether decisions are followed through.Can people see discipline in the way public money is managed?Can communities point to problems that were identified, addressed and actually resolved?Can businesses plan with greater confidence?Can young people see a credible path forward?Can citizens ask questions and receive answers?This is where leadership becomes serious.Delta State does not lack intelligent people, professionals, entrepreneurs, farmers, workers or young talent.What we need is a government capable of setting priorities, executing them properly and accepting responsibility for the outcome.That requires more than political experience.It requires competence.As 2027 approaches, perhaps the conversation should change from:“What will you promise us?”to:“How will you govern us—and how will we know you succeeded?”That is a question every candidate should be prepared to answer.What is the one thing you would use to judge the next Delta governor after four years in office?#IsaacEshor #Delta2027 #AAC #DeltaState

title: Tinubu’s FAAC Boom Is A Scam — Atiku

Thread Title: Tinubu’s FAAC Boom Is A Scam — Atiku

Main Post: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused the Federal Government of dressing economic decline in bigger naira figures, declaring that the much-celebrated FAAC “boom” is a monetary illusion that collapses once the figures are tested against currency depreciation, inflation, purchasing power and the mounting liabilities of state governments.In a statement issued by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said Nigerians should not be deceived by the spectacle of trillions being announced every month when the naira in which those trillions are denominated has lost enormous value and ordinary citizens are paying substantially more for virtually everything.“The arithmetic is brutal. In 2019, FAAC distribution was approximately ₦7.85 trillion, worth about $25.6 billion at the prevailing exchange rate. By 2025, FAAC had risen on paper to approximately ₦21.9 trillion, yet its dollar value had fallen to roughly $14.6 billion. So while government parades almost three times as many naira, the underlying dollar value is more than 40 per cent lower.“That is not an economic miracle. That is money illusion. You cannot batter the currency, allow inflation to ravage purchasing power and then wave bigger naira figures before Nigerians as evidence that the country has become richer. Bigger numbers do not cancel smaller value.”Atiku said the deception becomes even clearer when translated into the everyday experience of the Nigerian worker, where salaries may have increased nominally while their real value and purchasing power have deteriorated."Take the minimum wage as the simplest example. In 2019, ₦30,000 was worth roughly $83. By May 2023, that same ₦30,000 was worth about $65. Today, government boasts that the minimum wage has more than doubled to ₦70,000, yet at an exchange rate of around ₦1,320 to the dollar, that ₦70,000 is worth only about $53. Think about that: the number written on the worker’s payslip has risen from ₦30,000 to ₦70,000, but its dollar value has fallen from about $83 to about $53.“That is Tinubu’s money illusion in its simplest form. The figure in your hand is bigger, but the value in your pocket is smaller. A worker can earn more naira today and still afford less food, less transport, less electricity, less medicine and less housing than before. Government counts the naira but conveniently refuses to count what the naira can buy.”Atiku said the proper test of an economy is therefore not the size of the figures announced after FAAC meetings, but what those allocations can actually purchase and what obligations they are capable of meeting.“If FAAC is truly booming, then where is the boom? Where is it in the price of food? Where is it in transport? Where is it in electricity, healthcare, housing and jobs? Where is it in the purchasing power of salaries? Government cannot become richer on paper while the people become poorer in reality and then expect Nigerians to applaud the contradiction.”He said the contradiction becomes even more glaring when the debts still carried by states are placed beside claims of unprecedented revenue.“And here is another question the FAAC cheerleaders must answer: if the states are swimming in unprecedented revenues, why are they still drowning in debt? A September 2026 report based on Debt Management Office data shows that just 12 states whose governors are approaching the end of their tenures carry a combined debt burden of approximately ₦5.3 trillion, comprising ₦2.16 trillion in domestic debt and about $2.33 billion in foreign obligations.“So spare Nigerians the victory parade. You cannot boast endlessly about unprecedented FAAC allocations while states remain heavily indebted, pension and gratuity obligations persist, contractors chase payments and governments continue to carry enormous liabilities. If the money is as unprecedented as we are constantly told, Nigerians have every right to ask the most elementary question: where has the money gone?“What is the purpose of a revenue boom if liabilities remain enormous? What is the meaning of record allocations if governments continue borrowing and citizens cannot see a corresponding improvement in their standard of living? Revenue is not an achievement merely because it enters a government account. The achievement is what that revenue buys, what debts it settles, what infrastructure it delivers and how much better it makes the lives of the people.”Atiku said the administration must also stop pretending that fiscal discipline begins only when ordinary Nigerians require relief, insisting that government expenditure, tax concessions, import waivers, revenue exemptions, duplicated projects, abandoned projects and other areas of potential waste must be subjected to the same scrutiny.[LINK]

His latest tirade against the Federal Government’s fiscal triumphs is nothing more than a masterclass in political hypocrisy and desperate economic distortion.Atiku’s critique relies on a lazy, dishonest gimmick: evaluating Nigeria’s sovereign domestic economy entirely through the lens of the US Dollar. By doing so, he insults the intelligence of Nigerians and deliberately obfuscates the massive structural rot his own political era helped create. 1. The Hypocrisy of a Ghost Reformer* The Rebuttal: For years, Atiku campaigned on the promise that he would eliminate the corrupt fuel subsidy regime and unify the exchange rate market "even if they killed him." Civil servants buy food, pay school fees, and rent houses in Naira.* The Reality: By benchmark-pricing Nigeria’s minimum wage and state allocations entirely in USD, Atiku betrays his elite worldview— one that views Nigeria only through the lens of foreign capital and overseas spending. The ₦21 trillion FAAC distribution represents real, tangible local liquidity that is building roads, funding schools, and paying teachers across 36 states—things that cannot be wished away by Atiku’s arbitrary currency conversions.3. Unmasking the "Subsidy Illusion" of 2019* The Rebuttal: Atiku nostalgic reference to 2019’s FAAC figures is an admission of guilt. The "cheap dollars" and lower Naira numbers of 2019 were an artificial, unsustainable hallucination funded by trillions of Naira in bleeding subsidies that nearly bankrupted the country.* The Reality: The previous status quo was a ticking financial bomb. The Tinubu administration chose to diffuse that bomb, redirecting funds from the pockets of billionaire fuel smugglers and arbitrage traders directly to state and local governments. Calling the recovery of these stolen trillions a "monetary illusion" proves Atiku would prefer to feed the syndicates than fund the states.4. Intellectual Dishonesty on State Debts* The Rebuttal: Atiku points to state debts to claim the revenue boom is fake. This is an embarrassing display of fiscal illiteracy from someone who chaired the National Economic Council.* The Reality: Debt is a function of capital development, not a sign of failure. The historic surge in FAAC allocations has given states the unprecedented capacity to actually service their debts while simultaneously investing in massive infrastructure projects. Atiku wants Nigerians to look at a state's liabilities while ignoring the new highways, agricultural hubs, and security networks those liabilities are building.5. Empty Rhetoric vs. Structural Actions* The Rebuttal: Atiku asks, "Where is the money going?" while ignoring the massive fiscal reforms staring him in the face.* The Reality: The money is going toward the Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) transport revolution that is slitting transport costs in half. It is going into the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) to ensure poor children go to university. It is going into the direct pockets of workers through a more than 130% increase in the minimum wage. It is going into plugging the systemic leakages that Atiku’s political associates historically exploited.Atiku Abubakar’s "brutal arithmetic" is nothing but brutal political opportunism. Having been repeatedly rejected at the polls by the Nigerian people, he is reduced to acting as a professional doomsayer. He attempts to wave away record-breaking revenue generation and institutional tax reforms because he cannot stomach the fact that this administration is successfully rewriting Nigeria’s economic foundations—foundations that his generation of politicians left decayed. Bigger numbers do mean bigger value when they represent real independence from predatory subsidies, and no amount of dollar-denominated gaslighting from Atiku's Dubai palace can change that reality.

title: Catholic Priest Governor & His "First Lady'. A Matter Of Principle And Priority
main_content:
Thread Title: Catholic Priest Governor & His "First Lady'. A Matter Of Principle And Priority

Main Post: CATHOLIC PRIEST GOVERNOR & HIS "FIRST LADY'.A Matter of Principle, Priority, and Public Trust.On Monday, 7 September 2026, the Governor of Benue State—a Catholic priest—formally commissioned an office for the Coordinator of the First Lady.Let us be clear: the office of the First Lady does not exist in the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. It is an extra-constitutional creation. The Governor himself is unmarried. One is therefore compelled to ask, with both gravity and clarity: on what constitutional, moral, or practical foundation is such an office being established and publicly inaugurated with the full weight of state authority?The individual occupying this role is a married woman, Her Excellency Hon. Scholastica Ben-Sor. That title—“Her Excellency”—appears on her official Facebook page. The elevation is deliberate and public. It is not an informal courtesy; it is presented as an official designation.Contrast this with a documented record of restraint. During his eight years as Governor of Anambra State, Mr. Peter Obi never styled his wife as First Lady, nor did he expend public resources to create, equip, or commission an office for her. That fact is verifiable. It reflects a deliberate choice about the proper limits of public office and public funds.The following day, armed thugs prevented Mr. Peter Obi from visiting the families of the 270 people killed in Benue State. The Governor stated that he was unaware of the visit. One must then ask, with equal seriousness: if a sitting Governor can claim ignorance of a high-profile visit concerning mass loss of life in his own state, is he also unaware that the office he has just commissioned finds no place in our Constitution?These are not minor procedural questions. They go to the heart of constitutional fidelity, the responsible use of public resources, and the moral consistency expected of those who hold both spiritual and temporal authority.The people of Benue—and of Nigeria—deserve governance anchored in the Constitution, not in invented titles and offices.By Timothy Ofoegbu investigative journalist.

title: Ardo Can’t Speak For North, Tinubu Will Defy 10% Prediction In 2027, DWI
main_content:
Thread Title: Ardo Can’t Speak For North, Tinubu Will Defy 10% Prediction In 2027, DWI

Main Post: The Democracy Watch Initiative (DWI), has rejected claims by Dr Umar Ardo that Northern Nigeria has been marginalised under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, insisting that the region will support the President’s re-election bid in the 2027 presidential election.DWI also dismissed Ardo’s prediction that Tinubu could secure less than 10 per cent of the northern vote in 2027, describing the projection as unsubstantiated and politically motivated.In a statement issued by the Deputy National Chairman of DWI, Hon. Musa Adam, was reacting to an interview granted by Ardo on Frontline, a radio programme in Ogun State, which was subsequently reported by ThisDay.DWI called on northern voters and Nigerians generally to reject what it described as the politics of division, blackmail and unsubstantiated statistics ahead of the 2027 elections.Adam said DWI considered Ardo’s assertions an attempt to create unnecessary alarm and exploit regional sentiments for political purposes.Adam said: “We dismiss that interview in its entirety as the bitter lamentation of a serial political failure, a man whose only remaining relevance is unnecessary alarmism and self-serving propaganda.“Dr. Umar Ardo is in no moral or political position to speak for the North. He is a failed politician who has been rejected repeatedly by the very people he now claims to represent. In his own Adamawa State, for example, his governorship ambition collapsed woefully in 2023.“He was roundly defeated at the polls. A man who could not win his own state, who could not deliver his own ward and LGA, has no right to tell northerners how and who to vote. Dr Ardo’s political career is a case study in opportunism and serial defection. In the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), he contested the governorship primaries multiple times and failed.”He also criticised Ardo’s political history, accusing him of repeatedly changing political parties in search of relevance.According to him, Ardo contested governorship primaries under the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), later joined the All Progressives Congress (APC), returned to the PDP and subsequently moved to the Social Democratic Party (SDP).He further dismissed the League of Northern Democrats (LND), associated with Ardo, describing it as lacking the electoral influence to determine the political choices of northern voters.Adam also rejected Ardo’s allegation that the Tinubu administration had “Yorubanised” federal appointments and favoured the South-West.He said: “The North remains fully represented at the highest levels: the Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima; the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu,; ministers of strategic ministries are from the North; and the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas. Critical parastatals and security institutions have northerners in key positions. “Federal character is being observed, and the North is not excluded. His allegation that releases of funds to ministries were tied to regions is unsubstantiated and deliberately misleading. Budget releases follow due process, project readiness and statutory allocations and not primordial identities. If Ardo has verifiable figures, let him publish them. But he has none. What he has is a bitterness that has consumed him since his electoral defeats. “The North is witnessing federal projects, agricultural interventions, security operations, road and rail infrastructure, and social investment programmes under the Renewed Hope Agenda. These are not southern projects; they are Nigerian projects, and the North is a major beneficiary.“His attempt to drag Kwara and Kogi into North-South is another diversion. The North Central is part of the North, and northerners are not so gullible as to be divided by a man who has never won an election. Ardo’s prediction that Tinubu will get less than 10 per cent of northern votes is a hallucination born of frustration. “In 2023, President Tinubu won several northern states. In 2027, northerners will consolidate their support for him because they have seen a President who is resetting Nigeria’s economy for the better. The removal of the fuel subsidy, the unification of exchange rates, tax reforms, student loans, the Compressed Natural Gas initiative, and massive infrastructure investment are painful but necessary reforms that will benefit the North and the entire country.“Northerners are not sheep. They cannot be herded by a man who has been rejected at the polls. They will not take instructions from a serial defector who has spent his career switching parties and losing elections. Dr. Ardo should face his own political irrelevance and stop insulting the intelligence of northern voters.“The DWI calls on all well-meaning northerners and Nigerians to reject the politics of division, blackmail and false statistics being peddled by Dr. Umar Ardo. The North is ready to support President Tinubu to consolidate on his Renewed Hope reforms that are resetting Nigeria’s economy for the better. Ardo’s 10 per cent fantasy will remain what it is: a fantasy.”

title: Tinubu's $460000 forfeiture, a civil-dispute matter, not criminal - Bayo Onanuga
main_content:
Thread Title: Tinubu's $460000 forfeiture, a civil-dispute matter, not criminal - Bayo Onanuga

Main Post: STATEHOUSE STATEMENTCLARIFICATION ON THE ONGOING FREEDOM OF INFORMATION ACT CASE IN WASHINGTON, D.C.The Presidency has noted recent speculative reports concerning an ongoing Freedom of Information Act case before the United States District Court for the District of Columbia.For clarity, the matter is a civil records-disclosure dispute under the United States Freedom of Information Act. It is not a criminal case against President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, nor has the court found him guilty of any criminal wrongdoing.Here is the background to the case, which comes 23 years after the American Consulate in Lagos, in a letter dated February 4, 2003, informed the then Inspector General of Police, Mr Tafa Balogun, that an FBI records check found no criminal arrest records, wants, or warrants for then Governor Bola Ahmed Tinubu.In 2022, Mr Aaron Greenspan, who is known to work with Nigerian opposition figures including David Hundeyin and Atiku Abubakar, submitted FOIA requests to several United States government agencies seeking records relating to President Tinubu. After the agencies withheld certain records or declined to confirm or deny their existence, Mr Greenspan commenced Civil Action No. 23-1816 before the United States District Court for the District of Columbia in 2023.The court subsequently permitted President Tinubu to participate in the proceedings as an intervenor.During the proceedings, the Defendants asserted the "Glomar defence, a standard defence that US law enforcement agencies invoke from time to time. It simply means the government agency is not "in a position to deny or admit" the existence of an investigation. It protects government personnel and the techniques and sources law enforcement agencies use to investigate and prosecute crimes.Based on the invocation of this defence, the United States District Court granted summary judgment in favour of the CIA, EOUSA, Department of State, Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). It ruled that they be removed from the proceedings, leaving aspects of the claims involving the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Drug Enforcement Administration for further consideration.In compliance with the court’s orders, the FBI and DEA produced 399 pages of records, with portions redacted under exemptions provided by United States law. The Plaintiff challenged the FBI and DEA's decisions to redact portions of the documents produced.The FBI and DEA, through the United States Department of Justice (USDoJ), pushed back against the Plaintiff's requests. The FBI and DEA rejected the application to produce the documents without redactions for the following reasons:1. Some of the documents are protected from being revealed to the public by law, for example, Grand Jury proceedings. The law exempts transcripts of Grand Jury proceedings from public disclosure. The Pen Register Act also protects from disclosure information about certain court order(s) authorising or approving the installation and use of a pen register or trap and trace device. (FOIA Exemption 3)2. Some of the documents fall squarely within the attorney-work product and attorney-client privileges. Some documents contain instances where FBI and DEA agents sought and/or received legal advice from USDoJ attorneys. (FOIA Exemption 5)3. Some of the documents were prepared for law enforcement purposes. (FOIA Exemption 5)4. Some of the documents contain information which, if revealed, could lead to an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy. (FOIA Exemptions 6 and 7(C)).5. Some of the documents, if disclosed, will reveal the identities of confidential sources or compromise the techniques that law enforcement agencies use in investigating crimes. (FOIA Exemptions 7(D) and 7(E))President Bola Tinubu, on advice of his lawyers, has also asserted his rights as guaranteed by FOIA Exemption 7(C).The Plaintiff has until September 11, 2026, to file any opposition and reply to the Defendants' and Intervener's processes, while the FBI, DEA and the Intervenor have until September 18, 2026, to respond to the processes that the Plaintiff might have filed.The release or withholding of records under FOIA does not, by itself, establish criminal liability. The case concerns access to government records and the proper application of statutory exemptions.The Nigerian media should note that this case is exclusively within the control of Judge Beryl A. Howell of the United States District Court. She will determine its outcome, based on the evidence, applicable law, and the parties' arguments, not the wishful preference of Alhaji Atiku Abubakar or his agent, Mr Von Batten.Recent public commentary by Mr Karl von Batten has inaccurately portrayed him and his client as central to the proceedings. Neither is a party to the case.The litigation is a civil records-disclosure dispute under FOIA. It does not constitute a criminal charge, trial, or judicial finding against President Tinubu. The FBI and DEA have produced records with redactions, and the remaining question is whether those redactions are lawful.The United States District Court will decide that issue based on the filings and applicable US law, not political commentary.The Presidency therefore urges the media and the public to distinguish verified court proceedings from partisan speculation.Bayo OnanugaSpecial Adviser to the President(Information and Strategy)September 3, 2026

Thread Title: PETER OBI Visit, Before You Blame The Idoma In Benue State

Main Post: Tivs are not our brothers, there is no history that traced our ancestory or migration to the same point or parentage; there is a sharp contrast in the spoken languages, culture, tradition or even names. We have brothers in Ette, Enugu State; Olamaboro in Kogi State; Yalla in Cross River State; Doma, Keana and Obi LGAs of Nasarawa State and some parts of Delta where VDM comes from and part of Edo. Even though we are not in the same state, but we are brothers and there is no way they would have treated us baldly the way Tivs treat us, if we were to be in the same state; you know why - Their blood is ticker than Water (River Benue).What Idoma and Igede share with Tivs is neighborhood and not brotherhood. You guys are our neighbours and you treat us as such. We are just casualties of geographical contraptions and it has its far reaching effects on our collective existence as a people, either politically, economically or communally.How else do you explain that you have been in the same state with your "brothers" for 50 terrible years, yet, non of your "brothers" is qualified enough to be Governor or Speaker for 24 hours. I mean 24 hours (1 day). When Aodona was suspended last year as Speaker, I saw how our "brothers" hurriedly convoked a plenary on a Sunday and within one hour, installed my friend, Berger as Speaker, so that an Idoma "brother", Lami won't become acting Speaker for one day, even though she was constitutionally empowered to be acting Speaker, owning to the fact that she was a deputy Speaker - a loyal one at that.Since Fr. Alia is a Priest and won the "erection" without a wife, we expected that the fate of 1992 when Late Fr. Moses Adasu was a Governor and a "brother", Late Yakubu Agada was his deputy and his wife was made to oversee the office of the First Lady, would have come to play. But Alia did not only deny us that privilege, he also went ahead to mandate a Special Adviser to coordinate the Office of the First Lady, even though the state also has a Commisioner for Women Affairs, but because she is a " brother", she was not qualified, but a Junior officer, was.What about Secretary to the State Government? Idomas are no longer qualified, but our Tiv "brothers". It took the effort of Governor Ortom to break the jinx and created history, for appointing the first ever Chief Justice of Benue State who was an Idoma "brother". Imagine judiciary that has an established rules of appointing Chief Justices based on seniority, we reduced it to clannish relay, just as we are rotating the governorship amongst the 5 clans of Tiv, while your Idoma and Igede "brothers" are always used during the Guber elections to make the 2/3rd determinant as required by the Constitution.The worst of all these brotherhood is the fact that Idoma cannot be a Vice Chancellor of the State University and that of Federal University of Agriculture. To make it milder, Idoma cannot even be an SUG President of their own State owned University. Even Course Reps, it has to be that a "brother" is the HOD before another "brother" can become a Class Rep. It's as bad as that.Now, tell me my "brother", aside geography, what other indices qualifies an Idoma man to be refered to as "brother" by a Tiv man? This is a topic I have long refrained from. Check my publication titled: 'Continuous Marginalization of Idoma People: An Intolerable Impunity' published by almost all major newspapers in Nigeria in 2016, that's ten years ago. Google it. You would find in that article, how our late Och'Idoma lamented when he was seeking admission for his nephew at BSU and he personally recommended him, but he was still denied the admission, despite scoring far above the cutt-off points. That was a man who was not only a Paramount Ruler in Benue State, he was also himself a Pro Chancellor of a Federal University in another state.I suffered same fate in BSU. I wrote JAMB 5 consecutive years and insisted it must be Law and it must be BSU. Five terrible years I wasted writing JAMB, hoping that my own state university could be kind to a "brother" and offer him admission. Mind you, each JAMB result slip is still with me and there was no one I scored less than 220 marks, there was one particular year, maybe 2002, I had 235 marks, whereas, the cut off marks was just 120. A Terkura from Kwande who struggled to pull 130 marks, just 10 marks above the cut off, was offered admission that year to study law. That "brother" is now a lawyer and has almost 20 years post bar experience.So, my dear neighbor, I feel more comfortable when you call me neighbor and not brother.CCseun lalasticalaMynddNlfpmodDominiqueFergie001

title: Filth: Sanwo-olu Declares State Of Emergency On Waste Management
main_content:
Thread Title: Filth: Sanwo-olu Declares State Of Emergency On Waste Management

Main Post: To deploy 160 new compactor trucks, five transfer stations by Q2 2027LAGOS — Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has declared a “state of emergency” on waste management in the state, citing mounting pressure on waste collection and the growing menace of indiscriminate dumping across the metropolis.The governor, however, unveiled short-, medium- and long-term measures aimed at clearing the current backlog of waste and improving the state’s waste management system.Sanwo-Olu, who spoke on Wednesday during an inspection tour of the Olusosun dump site in Ojota, Lagos, said the intervention became necessary following weeks of slow waste turnaround and what he described as uncoordinated advocacy.The governor was accompanied by his deputy, Dr Obafemi Hamzat; Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab; and other senior government officials.“What we are seeing at Olusosun is a typical sight of the challenge. We are here to see what the problem is and to clearly declare a small state of emergency so that we can get out of this very unpleasant situation,” Sanwo-Olu said.He disclosed that the state government, in partnership with development partner Zoomlion, was constructing two new 2,400-metric-tonne Transfer Loading Stations at Olusosun and Solu 3 in Alimosho Local Government Area.According to him, the facilities would receive compacted waste before transferring it to two Material Recovery Sites under construction at Oke Osho in Epe and Erikitte in Badagry.“Each transfer station is designed to handle about 500 trucks per day. With the transfer loading stations, waste will be compacted and eventually taken to a material recovery site where it will be further sorted and broken into other uses,” he said.Sanwo-Olu projected that physical development on the facilities would become visible by the end of the year, while full operations were expected between the first and second quarters of 2027.For immediate relief, he said the state planned to increase the capacity of the Olusosun facility from between 250 and 350 trucks daily to between 350 and 450 trucks by increasing the number of tipping points from two or three to four or five.He added that road stabilisation work was underway at Solu 3, with grading expected to be completed within two to three weeks to allow continued waste reception.Similar stabilisation work, he said, was planned for Iwulepe in Ikorodu and Oke Osho in Epe.“We are hoping that before the end of next month, or in another six weeks, we will have four active dump sites: Olusosun, Solu 3, Iwulepe, and Oke Osho in Epe. And also a fifth one in Badagry, Erikitte,” the governor said.He explained that the additional disposal points would help reduce truck turnaround time, which could currently take as long as 12 hours, to only a few hours by providing closer disposal options.160 new compactors comingOn waste collection, Sanwo-Olu disclosed that the state government had ordered 160 new compactor trucks, with shipment expected to commence soon.“Landfill compactors for on-site compaction are also being procured,” he added.The governor said Zoomlion and Private Sector Participants, PSPs, would also procure additional trucks, while the state government would work with the operators to develop financing models that would enable them to expand their operations sustainably.The Chairman of the PSP Association, who joined the inspection tour, also agreed to a membership audit aimed at identifying inactive operators.The state government said although about 800 PSPs were registered, only an estimated 400 were effectively operating.“We don’t want to have 800 PSPs when it is actually only 400 that are effective,” an official said, adding that the exercise would create room for new investors.Sanwo-Olu also appealed to residents and tenement occupiers to pay for waste collection services.“Lagosians in particular, we just want service. We don’t want to pay for this service. I think this era has to stop. It’s so unfair to see people rendering service and people are not paying them,” he said.[LINK]

title: DID YOU KNOW? NNPC Is Rolling Out 50+ Self-service Stations
main_content:
Thread Title: DID YOU KNOW? NNPC Is Rolling Out 50+ Self-service Stations

Main Post: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited has disclosed that it plans to open between 50 and 70 smart self-service filling stations across Nigeria within the next 6 months.Executive vice-president of downstream at the NNPC Dr. Mumuni Dagazau announced this Thursday 10 September 2026 in Abuja at the commissioning of a self-service station with an electric vehicle (EV) charging facility.Dagazau said the initiative is aimed at transforming conventional filling stations into energy hubs that will offer multiple energy and mobility services.“This is the first of many smart stations we are going to have around the country. We are trying to turn from a filling station to an energy hub, and we are rolling out a lot of stations. I think even in Abuja, for this type of station, we have about 4 or 5,” he said.“We are hoping to roll out a significant number, about 50 to 70 of these types of stations, within the next 6 months. So this is what you’ll be seeing going forward from NNPC.”Dagazau said the energy hubs will combine different energy sources inclusive electricity, gas, and petrol, while also providing EV charging services.He said the new model will allow customers dispense petrol by themselves, including at night, using digital payment systems, while attendants will remain available to assist customers.SOURCE [LINK]

title: Why We Must Resist The Olodo Uprising In Imo State- Casmir Nweze
main_content:
Thread Title: Why We Must Resist The Olodo Uprising In Imo State- Casmir Nweze

Main Post: I stumbled across a supposed "open letter" addressed to Dr. Chima Matthew Amadi and the issues I saw raised there were so silly I almost burst out laughing. While it was funny in how it tried to split hairs over non-issues and words taken out of context, it was more concerning that this is the level that political commentary has been reduced to in Imo State. Nobody cares about the economy, the education or the security of Ndị Imo anymore, but they are only pressed about useless issues that have no bearing on the life and well-being of ndị Imo. One thing that stood out for me in that obvious hatchet job was the derision used to speak about Dr. Amadi's educational credentials, which would leave a heavy feeling in the chest of anyone who cares about the direction of public discourse in Imo State. What should have been a sober evaluation of campaign promises devolved into a bitter mockery of academic scholarship. It is disheartening to see public commentators deliberately strip away nuance to reduce a man's years of intellectual labor into a crude punchline just for the sake of a political witch hunt. Once political debate now resorts to belittling academic attainment, it is the entire society that loses as it watches the quiet erosion of its own core values.For decades, Imo State held a proud position as the intellectual heartland of Nigeria, consistently topping national literacy charts, joint admissions entrance exams, and academic indexes across the country. Education was our primary industry, our cultural pride, and our social ladder. To witness a public commentator dismiss a scholar as a "koromoto lecturer" simply to score a political point marks a painful fall from grace. It reveals a growing tolerance for anti-intellectualism in a state that built its entire reputation on academic excellence. In short, we are allowing the "Olodos" win, and woe betide us when they do! This decline in our collective respect for scholarship did not happen by accident. It coincides with a broader political era in Imo State, particularly under the administration of Governor Hope Uzodinma, where the prestige of deep intellectual preparation has been steadily displaced by raw political muscle and transactional governance. We have seen leadership that fails to model an appreciation for rigorous training and policy expertise, and the rest of the political ecosystem has simply followed suit. The result is a cline where political posturing is rewarded, while those who possess genuine academic credentials face ridicule for acquiring them.I have never met Dr. Chima Amadi, nor am I involved in his political campaign. I have my issues with him, but I would be lying if I said he is not what Imo needs at the moment, which is someone that understands our problems at a fundamental level. Compared to the rest of the rabble-rousers seeking political office in Imo State, he might as well be Einstein. My first awareness of Dr. Amadi's reputation was some years ago, while attending a program at the London School of Economics. During a conversation with a professor there, the man noticed I was Nigerian and asked if I knew Dr. Chima Matthew Amadi, describing him as one of the most brilliant individuals he had encountered. He noted how smoothly Amadi had transitioned his focus from a food-related field into public policy and economics, adding that he knew Amadi was from Nigeria. Discovering afterwards that this scholar praised in the halls of LSE was a fellow son of Imo State brought me an immense wave of pride, reinforcing my thoughts that our state was still capable of producing world-class minds.To see that same academic reputation dragged through local political mud is tragic. Dismissing international scholarship because it does not fit neatly into local political structures reflects a shallow understanding of intellectual value. A society that ridicules its scholars for daring to do things differently simply tells its finest minds to remain in exile. When political commentators degrade scholarship for cheap points, they harm the state far more than any political candidate, and that is why I am angry at the nerve of people who lick Hope Uzodinma's boots daring to mock academic excellence that was not bought at the backyard like some people we know. Imo State must search its heart and consciously choose to elevate cultured individuals who understand human capacity building through education. Complex governance challenges require deep intellect and policy understanding, not noise. Dr. Chima Amadi brings a level of intellectual exposure that deserves evaluation on its merits without the distraction of petty slurs. Imo citizens should hear him out, disregard coordinated attacks by paid attack dogs, and engage with a man who clearly understands a thing or two about leadership and knowledge.By Casmir Nweze.[LINK]

Main Post: WHEN LEADERSHIP REMEMBERS: THE MARK ESSET EXAMPLEBy Saviour Umana “The true measure of a leader is not only found in the heights he attains, but in his willingness to remember the hands that helped him climb.”There are moments in public life when an event transcends its immediate circumstances and speaks to something deeper about the character of leadership. Such moments are not always found at political rallies, legislative debates or the commissioning of public projects. Sometimes, they emerge from the quiet but powerful decision of a leader to remember those who have served faithfully, stood loyally and remained committed through the years. The recent decision of the Member representing Uyo/Uruan/Nsit Atai/Ibesikpo Asutan Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Hon. Mark Udo Esset, PhD, to reward some of his long-serving aides and staff with ₦43 million and two mini buses was one such moment, offering a revealing insight into a leadership philosophy that places value on loyalty, service, gratitude and the people behind every political journey.At a breakfast meeting hosted at his residence in Uyo, Rep. Esset brought together individuals who had served with him in different capacities and rewarded them in recognition of their years of dedication. The beneficiaries included security personnel, political associates, domestic staff and other aides whose services had contributed in different ways to the lawmaker's journey. While the financial value of the rewards naturally attracted attention, the deeper significance of the gesture lay in the message behind it: that those who serve faithfully should not become forgotten simply because their contributions are made away from the public spotlight.Among the beneficiaries was Supol Nsikak Udo of the Nigeria Police Force, whose experience provides perhaps one of the clearest illustrations of the relationship between the lawmaker and those who have served around him. Udo joined Esset's security detail as a Corporal and rose through the ranks to become a Superintendent of Police. When police personnel attached to public office holders were withdrawn during the nationwide exercise, he was also withdrawn from the lawmaker's security detail. The end of the official assignment, however, did not bring an end to the relationship. Rep. Esset subsequently recalled him in recognition of his loyalty and steadfastness and, at the recent gathering, rewarded him with ₦5 million. It was a gesture that suggested that genuine appreciation need not be dictated by the changing circumstances of official assignments.The lawmaker's appreciation extended to others who had worked with him over the years. His gateman, Mr. Christian Inyang, received ₦2 million, while his laundryman, Mr. Solomon Jacob, received ₦3 million. Mr. John Benjamin and Insp. James Anietimfon each received ₦5 million, while Mr. John Nyong received ₦3 million. Mr. Nsisong Etukudo, Mr. Iniobong Slimekere Ekere Ekere, Mr. Eyo Peter Okon and Mr. Aniekan Peters each received ₦5 million, while Mr. Jacob Asuquo and Mr. Ubong Charles received mini buses. The range of beneficiaries was particularly significant because it showed that recognition was not reserved for those occupying the most prominent positions. People who served in different capacities, including roles that rarely attract public attention, were also remembered.That human dimension became even clearer when Mr. Eyo Peter Okon spoke on behalf of the beneficiaries. Okon, whose relationship with Rep. Esset began in 2006, described his years of association with the lawmaker as life-changing and recalled how the relationship had contributed to important milestones in his personal life, including marriage and the building of his own house. His testimony offered a perspective that statistics alone cannot capture. Behind every political structure are human stories, and behind every successful journey are individuals whose sacrifices, loyalty and contributions may never be visible to the wider public. The decision to recognise such people was therefore as much a reflection of character as it was an act of generosity.Speaking at the event, Rep. Esset urged the beneficiaries to remain diligent, committed and dedicated to their duties, stressing that loyalty, hard work and the willingness to give one's best ultimately attract recognition and reward. The message carried significance beyond the immediate gathering. In any organisation or institution, people are more likely to give their best when they know that commitment is valued and good work does not go unnoticed. Appreciation strengthens relationships, encourages excellence and creates confidence that service has meaning.For Rep. Mark Esset, however, the principle of empowering and supporting people extends beyond those within his immediate circle. His representation of Uyo/Uruan/Nsit Atai/Ibesikpo Asutan Federal Constituency has included interventions directed at different categories of constituents. Students have benefited from educational support, petty traders and small business operators have received assistance, while women and youths have been provided with training and empowerment opportunities. Agricultural initiatives have also created opportunities for constituents seeking to build sustainable livelihoods, alongside employment facilitation and other interventions aimed at expanding access to economic opportunities.One of the more notable examples of this approach was the lawmaker's initiative to provide ₦1 million each to a male and female beneficiary from each of the 42 wards in the federal constituency. Beyond the monetary value, the initiative reflected an effort to take the benefits of representation closer to the grassroots and ensure that support was distributed across the constituency rather than concentrated in a few areas. It demonstrated an understanding that a federal constituency is ultimately made up of communities and individuals whose circumstances may differ, but whose expectations of meaningful representation remain the same.It is against this wider background that the ₦43 million reward and two mini buses can be viewed. The gesture was not an isolated departure from Rep. Esset's approach to public service, but another expression of a philosophy that places people at the centre of his understanding of leadership. Whether it is a student struggling to remain in school, a trader seeking capital, a young person in need of skills, a farmer pursuing an agricultural venture or a long-serving aide who has demonstrated loyalty over many years, the underlying principle remains the same: service should create value, commitment should be appreciated and people should be given opportunities to improve their circumstances.The lawmaker's approach also attracted commendation from political stakeholders at the event. The Member representing Nsit Atai State Constituency in the Akwa Ibom State House of Assembly, Hon. Prince-Aniefiok Attah, commended Rep. Esset for recognising and rewarding loyalty and dedication, while recalling the influence of the federal lawmaker's counsel on his own political journey. The Executive Chairman of Nsit Atai Local Government Council, Hon. Prince Anthony Nyong, similarly described Esset as a role model and a rewarder of good work. Their remarks pointed to another dimension of political leadership that is sometimes overshadowed by the pursuit of office: the ability to influence, mentor and positively shape the journeys of others.Ultimately, the quality of representation is best measured by its impact on the people. Political competition will always produce differing opinions and interests, but beyond the noise, the fundamental questions remain straightforward: are opportunities being created, are young people being empowered, are students receiving support, are businesses benefiting and are communities experiencing tangible attention? These are the measures that give meaning to a mandate and provide a more enduring basis for assessing public office than political rhetoric alone.There is, undoubtedly, more work to be done. The needs of Uyo/Uruan/Nsit Atai/Ibesikpo Asutan Federal Constituency remain substantial, unemployment continues to challenge many young people, businesses require sustained support and communities continue to look towards greater development. Yet meaningful progress is rarely achieved through isolated interventions; it is built through sustained commitment and continuity. Rep. Esset's description of the reward ceremony as only “a tip of the iceberg,” together with his assurance that he would continue to consolidate on the gains and dividends of his representation, therefore places the gesture within a broader commitment to sustaining and expanding the work already underway.For the people, effective representation also requires cooperation and responsible use of opportunities created through public service. Where empowerment is provided, beneficiaries must turn it into productive activity. Where training is facilitated, the skills acquired must translate into meaningful outcomes. Where financial support is given, it should serve its intended purpose. The strongest form of development occurs when public leadership and the people recognise that progress is a shared responsibility.The breakfast meeting in Uyo will therefore be remembered for more than the ₦43 million and two mini buses presented to the beneficiaries. It will be remembered as an occasion when a political leader publicly demonstrated that he had not forgotten people who had worked with him over many years. It was a statement about gratitude in public life and a reminder that those who contribute quietly to a leader's journey deserve recognition just as much as those who occupy the most visible positions.In a political environment where relationships can sometimes be valued only for their immediate usefulness, Rep. Mark Udo Esset has made a different statement through his actions. He has demonstrated that loyalty can be remembered, hard work recognised and service appreciated. His continuing investments in constituents, alongside his willingness to reward those who have served faithfully around him, present a picture of leadership that understands one of the enduring truths of public life: no leader succeeds alone.Perhaps that is the enduring lesson of the Mark Esset example. Leadership is ultimately about people, and the strongest legacy of public service is not simply the office occupied or the influence acquired, but the lives touched and the people who can look back and say that their contributions mattered. Long after money has been spent and political offices have changed hands, the impact of genuine appreciation and a life positively touched can remain. That is why a leader who remembers people does more than reward the past; he strengthens the values upon which meaningful leadership is built.#MarkOfEffectiveRepresentation#MarkOfTheGreenChamber#UyoFederalConstituency

title: APC Members Defect To NDC In Delta State
main_content:
Thread Title: APC Members Defect To NDC In Delta State

Main Post: The Nigeria Democratic Congress has received more than 1,000 defection letters from members of the All Progressives Congress across the Delta North Senatorial District ahead of the 2027 general elections.The figure was disclosed by the former Convener of the Delta Coalition for Equity, Chief Alex Ikpeazu, who led the defectors into the NDC during a formal reception in Agbor, Ika South Local Government Area of Delta State, on Monday.Ikpeazu said the group had received more than 1,000 letters from APC members indicating their intention to leave the party and join the NDC.He said the development reflected growing dissatisfaction among some APC members and political stakeholders in Delta North, particularly over what he described as years of marginalisation, deprivation and neglect of the senatorial district.“We have received over 1,000 defection letters from people who want to join the NDC,” Ikpeazu said.The defectors comprised former party leaders, political stakeholders and members of the Delta Coalition for Equity.They pledged to mobilise their supporters for the NDC ahead of the 2027 elections, particularly for the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and its Delta State governorship candidate, Yovwaye Chris.Receiving the new members, the NDC state chairman, Dr Oyidobo Richmond, described their arrival as a major boost to the party’s structure in Delta State.Richmond urged the defectors to return to their respective wards and local government areas and begin grassroots mobilisation ahead of the elections.He assured them that the party would treat all members equally, regardless of when they joined the NDC.[LINK]

title: FG Borrowing Like Drunken Sailor Despite Revenue Windfall – Atiku
main_content:
Thread Title: FG Borrowing Like Drunken Sailor Despite Revenue Windfall – Atiku

Main Post: Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has accused the Federal Government of reckless borrowing despite a windfall in oil revenue, saying the administration of President Bola Tinubu has continued to pile up domestic debts at a time crude oil prices have soared well above the benchmark used for the 2026 budget.In a statement issued by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the former vice president said it was troubling that the government would borrow ₦24.7 trillion domestically between January and August 2026 even as it enjoys higher earnings from crude sales.He described the scale of the borrowing as unprecedented, noting that it represented a 90.5 per cent increase over what was borrowed in the same period of 2025.“At the beginning of this fiscal year, the Federal Government budgeted on an oil benchmark of $64.85 per barrel. Today, crude oil prices have risen substantially above that benchmark.“Yet, instead of this windfall translating into lower borrowing, stronger businesses and relief for Nigerians, the Federal Government went into the domestic market and borrowed a staggering ₦24.7 trillion between January and August 2026 — 90.5 per cent more than the ₦12.98 trillion borrowed in the corresponding period of 2025.“This is not fiscal management. This is a government borrowing like drunken sailors in the middle of a revenue windfall”, he said.The former vice president argued that the various reform measures introduced by the Tinubu administration, including the removal of the petrol subsidy and the floating of the naira, ought to have eased pressure on government finances rather than deepened dependence on borrowing.“So the question Nigerians must ask again is very simple: where is the money going?“What makes this recklessness even more damaging is that government is now competing directly with Nigerian businesses for money. Credit to government grew by 43 per cent, while credit to the private sector grew by only 9.6 per cent. Government credit is expanding about 4.5 times faster than credit to businesses.“This government is not merely borrowing money; it is borrowing away the future of Nigerian businesses.“Nigeria cannot achieve prosperity by allowing government to swallow the credit that should finance production. An economy grows when businesses borrow to build factories, farmers borrow to expand production and entrepreneurs access affordable capital to create jobs — not when government becomes the biggest and most voracious customer in the banking hall.“My administration will impose fiscal discipline, cut waste, prioritise productive expenditure and progressively reduce government’s suffocating dependence on the domestic credit market.“Government must make room for the private sector to breathe, invest, produce and employ”, he stated.[LINK]

However, notwithstanding my support for President Obasanjo's nomination for a second term, the President after the nomination, acted very shabbily towards me.When I met him soon after the convention, he told me that he had learned that I had put forward the view that he was unsellable, unmarketable and unelectable. He then vowed that he was going to make sure that I was unsellable, unmarketable and unelectable.[LINK] Camp - Visit Wikileaks and type the following in the search bar NIGERIA: DID VP ATIKU OUTFOX BABANGIDA AND OBASANJO DURING THE PDP CONVENTION?According to Adesanya, Atiku met the governors the first day of the convention; they urged him to leave Obasanjo and seek the nomination himself. Atiku demurred; he also deflected the suggestion that he join Ekwueme. Finally, Atiku arranged a meeting between Obasanjo and the now irate governors. The governors railed that Obasanjo was hypocritically pursuing them for corruption, while turning a blind eye to corrupt politicians within his own Administration. Atiku supported the governor's position, telling Obasanjo that significant corruption was not the exclusive ambit of the governors and that serious transgressions occurred in the executive branch: he said it would be unjust to focus exclusively on gubernatorial excesses. Assuming the role of mediator, Atiku then asked both sides to affirm their mutual support and cease the antagonism being fueled by elements that wanted to destroy the PDP. The governors agreed to bury the hatchet, if Obasanjo would shelve the dossiers. Having demonstrated his influence with the governors, Atiku continued to play coy with Obasanjo.In the end, Atiku extracted an extraordinary concession from the President. Obasanjo agreed to relinquish the entire domestic agenda to Atiku, including the appointment of key economic policy-makers. Since Obasanjo focused on the world arena during his first term and aspired for recognition as an international statesman, Atiku said that is where he would like Obasanjo's attentions to remain. Obasanjo would serve the role of a "super Foreign Minister" and ceremonial Head of State. As Adesanya understood the agreement, Atiku would be allowed to direct domestic economic policy while Obasanjo busied himself with debt relief, NEPAD, conflict resolution and other measures to shore up Nigeria's image abroad.OBJ camp - visit Wikileaks and type the following in the search bar NIGERIA: DIFFERENT INSIDER VIEWS ON THE PDP CONVENTIONThe President was dazed, Abayomi recalled. Jarred by the unexpected possibility of defeat, the usually know-it-all Obasanjo eagerly solicited counsel on how to escape the closing vise. Early that day, the dominant theme was to seek a court injunction postponing the convention. Proponents suggested the delay to afford Obasanjo time to marshal support and undermine Ekwueme's momentum. However, this idea was ultimately discarded, partially because of apprehension over the public's reaction. More importantly, the push for an injunction became less urgent when the President's advisors began to sense their man was regaining ground by the hour.The President owed much of his recovery to his own tenacity and, at times, shamelessness. He pulled out virtually all the stops to clinch the nomination, according to Abayomi. For most of that day, the President's diet consisted of liberal portions of humble pie. The President pleaded and cajoled; on at least two occasions his eyes welled with emotion as he pursued fence-sitting delegates and governors. However, Obasanjo saved his best to keep Vice President Atiku from defecting.With rumor swirling that Atiku would opt to run with Ekwueme, Obasanjo wasted no time visiting the Vice President's residence. Obasanjo begged, declaring he would not leave Atiku's home unless the Vice President accompanied him to win back the delegates and governors. The performance had the desired effect. Atiku joined Obasanjo in publicly lobbying the conventioneers. While it might not have been Obasanjo's finest hour it was the defining moment of the convention. What had been a suspenseful contest would now turn into a rout.

title: Osun Constituents To Recall Senator Fadahunsi

Thread Title: Osun Constituents To Recall Senator Fadahunsi

Main Post: by Joshua Dada Youth groups and constituents of Osun East Senatorial District on Wednesday staged a peaceful protest over an alleged inciting comment credited to the Senator representing the district, Senator Francis Adenigba Fadahunsi, during the concluded 2026 Osun State governorship election, saying it is part of the process to recall him from the National Assembly.The youths under the aegis of Coalition of Osun East Youths, and Concerned Citizens, armed with placards with varying inscriptions, in their numbers thronged the streets of Ilesa as they converged at Enuwa roundabout, marched through Isokun, Ilesa Market Square and terminated the procession at the gate of Owa-Obokun palace.Fadahunsi had denied the comments he allegedly made in a viral video during a protest staged by the All Progressives Congress against the alleged killing of their members, saying that it was doctored by the opposition party to tarnish his image.Addressing newsmen on behalf of the protesters, Comrade Olorunfemi Olatunji explained that the protest was part of the recall process for Fadahunsi over the inciting comment, citing poor representation as one of the reasons for the protest.He scored the district Senator’s representation poorly and berated him for an incisive statement made during the 2026 electioneering period.According to him, “We, under the aegis of the Coalition of Youth and Students with Concerned Citizens of Osun East Senatorial District, are opposed to the reckless statement made by our Senator before the election.“This protest is the first stage of our actions.We are recalling him back home. We are still going to Abuja. All the necessary legal actions to recall him have been prepared, and we will begin them in a few days. “We have filed the petition, and we are following it with action that his recall process will follow.”Also, the Chairman of the National Youth Council of Nigeria (NYCN), Comrade Akinbode Olakolupo, called for the immediate arrest of the lawmaker.He said, “We demand a transparent, impartial and credible investigation into all credible allegations of incitement, threats, killings and political violence connected to the electoral process by Senator Fadahunsi.“We urge the police and security operatives to put radical efforts together to recover illegal firearms from political thugs and criminals.”[LINK] Youth Protest Over Statements by Senator Fadahunsi During Osun 2026 Governorship ElectionYouths in Ilesa, Osun State, staged a protest over concerns surrounding statements attributed to Senator Francis Fadahunsi during the 2026 Osun governorship election period,... pic.twitter.com/rUFTt0S036— The Daily Beam ([USERNAME]) September 9, 2026Pressure Mounts For Action Against Senator Fadahunsi Over Osun Gov'ship Election Comment pic.twitter.com/CDZtfkXz6k— Africa Independent Television ([USERNAME]) September 10, 2026

title: Adamawa:apc Loyalists Pass Vote Of Confidence On Rep. Aliyu Boya In Yola
main_content:
Thread Title: Adamawa:apc Loyalists Pass Vote Of Confidence On Rep. Aliyu Boya In Yola

Main Post: ....as he rallies Supporters to vote for Tinubu, Galadima, Promises Massive Empowerment, More Projects By Tom Garba, YolaThe member representing Fofure/Song Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Hon. Aliyu Wakili Boya, on Thursday addressed hundreds of APC supporters and party loyalists at his residence in Yola, assuring them of more dividends of democracy.The meeting, which drew party stakeholders, women and youth groups, was used to mobilize support ahead of the 2027 general elections.Hon. Boya assured the gathering that a large-scale empowerment program will be organized soon for his constituents.He said women, youths and party faithful will benefit from *motorbikes, tricycles, grinding machines and business capital to support small businesses and self-reliance.“We are not here to make empty promises. Very soon, we will roll out a huge empowerment that will touch every segment of our people,” Boya said.The lawmaker recounted his achievements in the National Assembly, saying his efforts have led to job opportunities for many young people in federal government agencies.He also listed key projects attracted to the constituency, including the establishment of a College of Health, College of Education, and the ongoing Jabba-Labba-Belel Road* that will link Adamawa to Cameroon.According to him, more development will come if the people re-elect him, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and the APC governorship candidate, Tijjani Galadima.“The re-election of the APC government from top to bottom is the answer to all your questions and the solution to all our problems. You will always see us and see the benefits,” he stated.Speaking on behalf of the supporters, Babangida Yerima passed a vote of confidence on Hon. Boya, describing him as “a man who leads with the people in mind.”“Boya has never failed us since he was Chairman of Fofure Local Government and now as a federal lawmaker. He is still standing on the pillar of a good leader who works only for the people and not himself,” Yerima said.“No wonder he is called Sardauna– a man for the masses and a servant of the people. We are passing a vote of confidence on him to continue representing us.”He added that the group will mobilize votes for Boya, President Tinubu and Galadima. “The young man is doing well, and as such we are going to mobilize votes for him, Tinubu and Galadima. He has convinced us to do APC and work for the party,” he said.The event ended with chants of solidarity and prayers for the success of the APC in 2027.

title: 2027: Sdp’s Adebayo Promises Solar Power On Every Nigerian Roof Within 11 Months
main_content:
Thread Title: 2027: Sdp’s Adebayo Promises Solar Power On Every Nigerian Roof Within 11 Months

Main Post: The presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Adewole Adebayo, has pledged to provide between 11 and 15 kilowatts of solar power for every Nigerian roof within 11 months of taking office if elected in 2027.Adebayo made the pledge on Tuesday during an interview on Arise Television’s Prime Time.“I promise that between 11 to 15 kilowatts of solar power will be put on every roof within 11 months,” he said.He said his administration would build solar-panel manufacturing plants across the country and train Nigerians to install and maintain solar power systems.According to him, the proposed solar clusters would supply electricity for basic household needs, generate employment and produce up to 32,000 megawatts.“You put all of that, and you generate employment, and you now generate up to 32,000 megawatts from these clusters that you do. Then you forget about it. I told them that the way we are going to manage the national grid.“National grid is a backup. In case a cluster fails, you will power from there,” Adebayo said.The SDP candidate said the factories could be established through partnerships with countries including China, Turkey and India, with Nigerians trained to operate them.He said he had previously advised the government on power-related matters and tested solar technology in his hometown, where he claimed to have trained about 2,000 people.“I did an experiment in my hometown. I have about 2,000 people I trained on solar, because I manufacture the solar panels myself. I do lithium battery.“The only thing I haven’t got the technological power to do is the inverter. So I buy the inverter. I do the solar battery,” he said.Adebayo also advocated government investment in strategic sectors, including aviation and manufacturing, arguing that such investments could be made through operating and maintenance contracts instead of leaving the sectors entirely to private operators.On electricity generation, he said his administration would promote domestic refining and tackle crude oil theft, which he identified as major challenges to energy security and economic growth.He claimed that up to 900,000 barrels of crude oil were still being stolen, saying the recovery of the oil would improve supply without requiring additional government spending.Adebayo further said public investment in sectors such as electricity and education could create jobs, as workers employed in those sectors would earn incomes.[LINK]

title: Court Orders INEC To Use Modified NDC Logo
main_content:
Thread Title: Court Orders INEC To Use Modified NDC Logo

Main Post: Henry Seriake Dickson [USERNAME] Party Members and Nigerians,It is our pleasure to announce that yesterday, the Federal High Court sitting in Abuja, presided over by Hon. Justice J. O. Abdulmalik, granted the prayers of the NDC in a suit seeking to compel the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to upload and utilise our modified digital logo, as contained in our party’s constitution, instead of the association logo with which the NDC was originally registered.The party had, at our first NEC meeting, approved and forwarded our modified logo to INEC, which subsequently uploaded it. However, without any reason communicated to us, INEC later removed the modified logo and insisted on using the old logo of the association, a position we disagreed with. After giving INEC sufficient time to correct the situation without any action taken, we were compelled to go to court.We therefore commend the judiciary for its timely intervention and welcome the judgment directing INEC to forthwith upload and utilise our modified digital logo. We commend the judiciary for upholding the party’s legitimate position and ensuring that due process is respected.We also commend all party members, particularly our candidates, for their patience and understanding throughout this period. We urge all candidates and party members to forthwith adopt and utilise the approved logo in all campaign materials, including banners, posters and other publicity materials.I want to assure everyone that the party has experienced and strategic leaders who understand what we are doing. Therefore, nobody should panic. Members are free to raise questions and concerns, but there is absolutely no reason for panic.We understand that some candidates and party members may have already made arrangements using the other logo, and we regret the inconvenience this may have caused. However, both logos retain the two-finger victory sign. Candidates should now transition to the logo approved in our party’s constitution, which is the authentic party logo and, indeed, the one that is more widely recognised.We regard the challenges surrounding this matter as part of the administrative machinations we have continued to confront. But we want to assure our members that we are democratic fighters. We do not run away from battles.We thank God that the judiciary has once again vindicated our position.Accordingly, from this moment, the party and all its candidates should use and refer to the constitutionally approved modified digital logo in all campaign and party-related materials.The party will issue a formal statement and embark on appropriate publicity to ensure that all members and candidates are properly guided, while also sensitising the voting public. There is still time to do so.We thank all our members, candidates and supporters for their patience, understanding and steadfastness.Together, we remain focused in SERVICE. Together, we move forward.NDC all the way!~HSDSource

Studying in Germany : What you should knowThis is in response to a FAQ I always get from scholars especially nairalanders.The first point of contact is this website:Daad.de/enThe website above contain almost all the university in Germany and some other sister universities around Germany.Most of the schools in Germany are tuition free even for international students, you only get to pay a certain amount as semester fees say between 100-400 euros and most times the semester fee comes with a semester ticket to aid in transportation in your city or town.However, before you're granted a student visa, you have to prove that you can take care of your living expenses with one of the following means ;1. Block account: The estimated living expenses for a student in a month is 720euros, when you multiply that by 12 months, you get 8640euros. This is the amount you're required to block in an already opened account with either Deutsch bank, Fintiba or Xpatrio. It is called a block account because you will not be able to withdraw everything at once, only 720euros will be released to you every month.2. Sponsorship letter: If you have a relative living and working legally in Germany, they can get you this letter. They'll have to visit the alien office in their city and will be required to provide some documents and pay a certain fee. The letter will be sent to you when they receive it so that you can go with it for your visa interview.3. Scholarship: This is usually the best if you have the scholarship, your visa will be granted in under 2 weeks after interview. So try and look for scholarships you can apply to.Now that you understand the financial situation, let's go into the application process.To search for schools, click on this link[LINK] your search to make it easier, there are English taught courses there.Generally, the very important documents needed to apply to schools in Germany are;1. Transcript2. English Proficiency3. School Certificates (Degree, Waec, etc)However, depending on the school, some other documents needed are as follows.4. Curriculum Vitae5. Motivation letter6. Reference letters7. GRE test8. Etcetera.. Visit your prospective school website and find out the documents they need from you.Note: You don't apply with your original documents, you have to make photocopies of them and Certify them in High court or a Notary public. If you stay in Lagos, you can certify at the German Embassy too. You'll have to book appointment for that.For those planning to go for a Bachelors course, you need a 100level transcript from a university to apply for a BSc program in Germany. WAEC alone will not be enough and No, OND will not do, you need a HND.For the application proper, it is always important to go through the website of the schools you want to apply to, you'll get a lot of information form there concerning how to apply.
